title: Learning-Augmented Fleet and Charging Infrastructure Co-Design under Vehicle-Level Cyclic Stability
affiliations: University of Michigan Ann Arbor and

detail.title: Learning-Augmented Fleet and Charging Infrastructure Co-Design under Vehicle-Level Cyclic Stability
detail.abstract: Electrification of large-scale fleet operations requires coordinated decisions over charging infrastructure investment, heterogeneous fleet composition, energy-constrained routing, and demand assignment. In depot-based systems, operational feasibility must also be repeatable across planning horizons, requiring vehicles to return to compatible terminal locations and energy states. We propose an integrated optimization framework for joint charging infrastructure placement, fleet sizing, routing with charging, and multi-commodity load assignment under explicit vehicle-level cyclic stability constraints. Each vehicle must return to its origin station at the end of the horizon, and electric vehicles must satisfy terminal energy compatibility, ensuring repeatable daily execution without exogenous repositioning or energy resets.We show that imposing cyclic stability fundamentally alters the operational problem. In its absence, the routing component reduces to a time-expanded network flow model; with stability, the feasible region is characterized by terminal-compatible tours, and pricing becomes a resource-constrained shortest path problem. Despite endogenous infrastructure decisions, we establish that the underlying combinatorial space of feasible stable tours is invariant across designs. This invariant column space with parametric feasibility enables principled cross-design information reuse within a decomposition framework.To solve the resulting large-scale mixed-integer program, we develop a learning-augmented Benders and column generation architecture that maintains a persistent tour pool and applies adaptive selection to control restricted master problem dimensionality while preserving exactness. Computational experiments on structured grid networks and large-scale Michigan instances demonstrate scalability, stable convergence behavior, and substantial computational gains from invariant-aware column management.

title: VOLGA-Hex: Validity-oriented pOlycube LabelinG for CAD models

detail.title: VOLGA-Hex: Validity-oriented pOlycube LabelinG for CAD models
detail.abstract: For many simulation codes, hexahedral meshes, and more specifically block-structured hexahedral meshes, remain preferred while their automatic generation is unsolved. To this purpose, we investigate the usage of a polycube-based approach. Starting from a tetrahedral mesh $T_\Omega$ of the domain of interest $\Omega$, we focus in this work on the labeling stage, which consists in assigning each boundary facet of $T_\Omega$ to one of the 6 signed principal axes $\{\pm {\bf X},\pm {\bf Y},\pm {\bf Z}\}$. Similar works are confronted with 2 challenges: over-constraining validity criteria, and the conflated processing of validity criteria with quality metrics. We tackle these obstacles with the definition of two automatic routines based on semi-global labeling operators. Our approach is successfully tested on CAD models, which are of interest for many numerical simulation problems. Comparing to some other approaches, we obtain a better rate of valid labelings, while being competitive on quality metrics and significantly faster.

title: Real-World Benchmarking of Control Strategies in an Industrial Energy System

detail.title: Real-World Benchmarking of Control Strategies in an Industrial Energy System

keywords.keywords: Control optimizationReinforcement learningModel predictive controlMarket-based controlMulti-agent system

detail.abstract: Industrial energy systems face increasing complexity driven by decarbonization requirements, renewable integration, and price volatility, making conventional rule-based control insufficient to exploit energy efficiency and flexibility potentials. Advanced control strategies can improve the operation strategy, yet their real-world performance and transferability remain largely unexplored due to inconsistent system representations and the absence of quantitative benchmarking frameworks. This work addresses these gaps by presenting ETA Factory Thermal System Operation (EFTSO), a framework for the development, benchmarking, and simulation-to-reality transfer of optimized control strategies for industrial energy systems. The application of the framework is demonstrated on a representative industrial heating network. A rule-based controller is used as baseline and compared with reinforcement learning, model predictive control, and a market-based controller. The evaluation metrics incorporate key performance indicators including energy efficiency, operating costs, security of supply, system wear, and CO$_2$ emissions. Real-world experiments over three representative days reveal that each advanced control strategy exhibits distinct trade-offs between competing objectives, while none achieves optimal performance across all metrics. Moreover, simulation results alone prove unreliable predictors of real-world behavior. Therefore, this study demonstrates the essential role of real-world validation in control strategy assessment and provides a framework to systematically benchmark different control approaches.

title: Navigating the Early Years: A Guide for New Faculty
affiliations: , University of Waterloo - School of Accounting and Finance and Wilfrid Laurier University - Accounting

detail.title: Navigating the Early Years: A Guide for New Faculty
detail.abstract: The transition from doctoral student to tenure-track assistant professor marks a critical juncture in an academic career. This conceptual commentary offers experience-based insights for early-career accounting faculty, addressing the distinct pressures of a discipline shaped by professional certification requirements, diverse institutional missions, and a rapidly evolving technological landscape. Drawing on practical observations and current literature, we address institutional variation, tenure expectations, research pipeline management, teaching responsibilities, service commitments, and professional identity formation. We further discuss the role of mentorship and professional associations in supporting career development, and offer strategies for navigating departmental politics, institutional fit, and the challenges of an academic environment increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence and data analytics. By surfacing both the spoken and the hidden rules of academic life, this paper serves as a practical guide for tenuretrack accounting faculty navigating the complexities of the assistant professorship.

title: A Tight Lower Bound for the Monopoly Revenue-to-Surplus Ratio under α-Regularity
affiliations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics - School of Information Management and Engineering and Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: A Tight Lower Bound for the Monopoly Revenue-to-Surplus Ratio under α-Regularity
detail.abstract: We generalize the classical lower bound for the monopoly revenue-to-surplus ratio under the monotone hazard rate (MHR) condition to a broader class of distributions satisfying the α-regularity condition. Specifically, we show that monopoly revenue is at least α 1 1-α of total surplus, and characterize the extremal survival functions attaining this tight bound. The result gives the exact surplus-extraction guarantee along the α-regularity spectrum, from zero under standard regularity to the classical 1/e benchmark in the MHR limit.

detail.abstract: Competition law stands as one of the most consequential instruments of economic governance, tasked with preserving market contestability in an era defined by unprecedented corporate consolidation and digital disruption. This paper undertakes a comparative jurisprudential examination of antitrust regulation across three distinct jurisdictions: the United States, the United Kingdom, and India. It scrutinises the statutory foundations and enforcement philosophies animating each regime, tracing the evolution from the century old Sherman Act to the contemporary Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 and the Indian Competition (Amendment) Act 2023. The analysis navigates two central pillars of competition law: the prohibition of dominant position abuse and the ex ante scrutiny of strategic acquisitions. A defining tension emerges between the conduct based American orthodoxy, the multifactorial prospective framework of the United Kingdom now fortified by a specialist Digital Markets Unit, and the rapidly evolving hybrid model adopted by India. The ascendancy of technology conglomerates commanding vast data reserves and controlling platform ecosystems has exposed the structural limitations of conventional merger thresholds calibrated for analogue markets. Ultimately, this paper argues that effective governance of digital markets cannot be achieved through purely retrospective enforcement. It advocates for a tiered, designation based framework that provides institutional agility and acknowledges competition law as a vital mechanism of democratic oversight uniquely positioned to restrain private power.

title: Boundedly Rational Meta-learning in Sequential Consumer Choice
affiliations: , University of Washington and University of Washington

detail.title: Boundedly Rational Meta-learning in Sequential Consumer Choice
detail.abstract: Many consumer decisions are repeated choices under uncertainty. Standard models capture these decisions using Bayesian learning and dynamic programming: consumers update beliefs from feedback and use those beliefs to guide future choices. In many markets, however, learning does not restart when consumers enter a new context: prior experience with a brand, product, or provider can shape beliefs in later, related decisions. We study this cross-context knowledge transfer, or meta-learning, in sequential choice. We design a hierarchical laboratory task in which participants repeatedly choose among airlines across routes and observe noisy binary outcomes. Reduced-form evidence shows that participants improve not only within routes, but also across routes: they choose better airlines earlier in later routes and reduce pseudo-regret. To identify the mechanism behind this transfer, we compare human choices to a no-transfer benchmark and a fully integrated Bayesian meta-learning benchmark. In particular, we introduce a class of boundedly rational meta dynamic programming policies, BRMDP(D), that approximate full integration using a limited number of hyper-posterior draws, denoted by D. Trial-bytrial likelihood comparisons show that low-D boundedly rational meta-learning, especially BRMDP(1), fits participant behavior better than both no transfer and fully integrated Bayesian transfer. Consumers, therefore, transfer brand-level regularities across contexts, but through coarse representations of prior uncertainty. The findings imply that models of consumer learning should allow for approximate cross-context transfer, and that managerial counterfactuals based on either no-transfer or fully integrated learning can be misleading.

title: Generative AI and Physician Productivity
affiliations: California State University, San Marcos and Emory University - Goizueta Business School

detail.title: Generative AI and Physician Productivity
detail.abstract: Clinical documentation imposes a significant burden on healthcare providers, consuming substantial clinician time and contributing to after-hours work that extends well beyond the clinical day. We study whether a rapidly diffusing generative AI application, ambient clinical documentation, can meaningfully reduce this burden. We partner with a large East Coast healthcare system that implemented an ambient AI tool across a range of outpatient settings and provider types. We link detailed adoption and utilization data to operational outcomes measured in the EHR: note activity time, total EHR time, after-hours documentation, and productivity measures tied to reimbursement, specifically relative value units (RVUs) and patient charges. Leveraging staggered adoption, we employ a difference-indifferences design complemented by models that exploit variation in utilization intensity. We find that adoption reduces note activity time by approximately 12% on average, with reductions exceeding 20% among higher-utilization adopters. The benefits arise immediately, extend to reductions in total EHR time and after-hours work, and are accompanied by increases in RVUs and charges. Effects are heterogeneous and scale with intensity of use. The largest gains accrue to less experienced clinicians, advanced practice providers, and primary care settings. Taken together, the findings provide strong evidence that ambient GenAI can simultaneously reduce administrative burden and improve operational and financial performance across a wide range of provider types and practice contexts.

title: Managing Scaling Tensions: The Case of Differentiation and Integration in Social Enterprises
affiliations: University of Hamburg and University of Hamburg

detail.title: Managing Scaling Tensions: The Case of Differentiation and Integration in Social Enterprises
detail.abstract: Scaling up is a key strategic challenge for social enterprises, organized as hybrid organizations, that pursue multiple, potentially conflicting goals (e.g., profit and social impact), because tensions arising from these conflicting goals become particularly salient in growth phases. Whereas differentiated hybrids exclude beneficiaries from value creation processes, rendering them as sole recipients of social value, integrated hybrids include beneficiaries, making them co-creators of social value. Based on a qualitative case study of 22 German social enterprises, we set out to elucidate how social enterprises, organized as differentiated or integrated hybrids, manage scaling tensions along the scaling process. We find that integrating beneficiaries into value creation, affects their prioritization of scaling strategies, what kinds of scaling tensions emerge and how they strategically respond to tensions throughout the scaling process. We build on a four-stage process model illustrating how the scalability of social enterprises is shaped by differentiation and integration at each stage, from setting goals and conceiving scaling strategies, to their execution and evaluation. Differentiation allows for stronger growth with a higher risk of mission drift, by prioritizing avoidance-based responses to tensions. Integration makes hybrids more perceptive to tensions, allowing for proactive, dialogue-based responses. With our findings we contribute to the extant literature on scaling up social enterprises, tension management in social enterprises and the literature on the influence of institutional settings on hybridity and scalability.

detail.abstract: We present an empirical audit of 292 sales-visible B2B small business websites measuring synthetic page experience metrics, mobile-versus-desktop performance asymmetry, and web accessibility conformance using a headless Chromium rendering pipeline. Across 191 sites with valid mobile Lighthouse evaluations, 86.4% post poor Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), only 5.2% post good LCP, and 14.5% post non-good Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). Combined across LCP, First Contentful Paint (FCP), and CLS as Lighthouse-measured page experience thresholds, 96.9% fail at least one and only 3.1% pass all three. We treat this as a synthetic-Lighthouse composite, not a Core Web Vitals composite as Google operationally defines that term, since the third Core Web Vital (Interaction to Next Paint) is field-measured and not captured here. The failure pattern is asymmetric: time-to-first-content metrics fail overwhelmingly while layout stability mostly passes. Across 165 sites with paired mobile and desktop runs on the same codebase, desktop performance exceeds mobile by a median of 22 Lighthouse points. Accessibility findings are categorical: every one of the 191 sites with valid axe-core evaluations failed the WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose check (axe-core rule link-name, severity: serious). We find that the modal failure mode is not generalized slowness but specifically time-to-first-content latency on mobile. Methodology, full dataset (n = 292, 41 columns, anonymized at row level), and reproduction details are released under CC BY 4.0.

title: Identity-Focused Instagram Strategies for Entrepreneurial Competitive Sustainability
affiliations: and Independent Researcher

detail.title: Identity-Focused Instagram Strategies for Entrepreneurial Competitive Sustainability
detail.abstract: In the contemporary digital economy, Instagram has evolved beyond a social networking platform into a strategic environment for entrepreneurial visibility, customer engagement, and long-term brand positioning. This study examines how identity-focused Instagram strategies contribute to entrepreneurial competitive sustainability in dynamic and highly competitive markets. The paper explores the relationship between entrepreneurial identity construction, authentic storytelling, visual branding consistency, audience interaction, and sustainable business performance. Drawing from recent studies on digital branding, social media marketing, and entrepreneurial communication, the research highlights how entrepreneurs use identity-driven content to establish trust, strengthen consumer loyalty, and differentiate themselves from competitors. The study further argues that sustainable competitiveness on Instagram depends not only on promotional activities but also on the entrepreneur's ability to communicate values, personality, credibility, and social relevance through continuous and meaningful engagement. In addition, the paper discusses the influence of algorithmic visibility, influencer collaboration, and community-centered branding in shaping long-term entrepreneurial resilience. The findings indicate that identity-focused strategies improve customer retention, increase perceived authenticity, and support adaptive marketing practices that enhance sustainability in digital entrepreneurship. The study contributes to the growing literature on social media entrepreneurship by providing a conceptual understanding of how identity-centered Instagram practices can support competitive advantage and sustainable entrepreneurial growth.

title: The Evolution of Bridge Maintenance: From Visual Inspection to AI-Driven Digital Twins

detail.title: The Evolution of Bridge Maintenance: From Visual Inspection to AI-Driven Digital Twins
detail.abstract: This article provides an overview of the ongoing transition from conventional bridge maintenance practices toward AI-driven and data-informed infrastructure management approaches. Bridge infrastructure worldwide is facing increasing pressure from aging structural systems, growing transportation demand, environmental deterioration, and limited maintenance resources. Conventional techniques used to maintain bridges have long relied on periodic visual inspection, which still remains important but comes with certain challenges such as subjectivity, limited inspection frequency, inaccessibility, and inability to continuously monitor the structural condition. Recently, bridge engineering has slowly begun to adopt data-driven maintenance procedures using technologies including Artificial Intelligence (AI), SHM, IoT, drones, and digital twins. In this article, the evolution of bridge maintenance is explored especially in terms of transitioning from the conventional inspection methods to those based on data and AI. Some of the technologies examined include digital twins, AI-powered inspection through drones, predictive maintenance, data analysis, and the importance of structural health monitoring among others. Some of the challenges encountered during this transition include cost, cybersecurity threats, interoperability problems, reliability of sensors, digital gap, and the need to prepare the maintenance workforce for change. Rather than portraying AI as a replacement for engineers, this article emphasizes that future bridge maintenance will depend on integrating engineering judgment with intelligent digital systems.

title: Beyond Token Prediction: Contextual Comprehension and Consequence-aware AI Architectures

detail.title: Beyond Token Prediction: Contextual Comprehension and Consequence-aware AI Architectures
detail.abstract:
This paper argues that the next stage of AI architecture should not be conceptualized primarily as larger language models, but as systems optimized for contextual comprehension, explicit knowledge integration, inconsistency handling, consequence anticipation, and auditable explanation. 

Drawing on foundation-model research, critiques of meaning-through-form alone, causal inference, neuro-symbolic AI, retrieval-augmented generation, and agentic systems, it proposes an operational definition of understanding as the capacity to maintain a task-relevant semantic state, ground claims in evidence, reason over constraints, evaluate action consequences, and produce explanations that remain traceably coupled to decision processes. 

On this basis, the paper introduces understanding-centric, consequence-aware architecture patterns, together with evaluation metrics and experimental protocols spanning language, reasoning, retrieval, contradiction handling, and action tasks. It also situates the broader LUM research stream as a historical research-program label inside the text while deliberately removing scale from the title and from the core definition of understanding. The resulting agenda is intended as a rigorous bridge between LLMs, SLMs, neuro-symbolic systems, and enterprise decision intelligence.

title: The Mid-Manager Institutional Protectorate: Coalition-driven Routine Preservation in Matrixed Multinationals

detail.title: The Mid-Manager Institutional Protectorate: Coalition-driven Routine Preservation in Matrixed Multinationals
detail.abstract: Matrixed multinational enterprises rely on middle managers to translate enterprise governance into local operational practice. This paper theorizes a stable middlemanagement layer that systematically converts standardization mandates into local accommodation, naming the pattern the institutional protectorate. Drawing on Nelson and Winter (1982) routines theory and Aghion and Tirole (1997) on formal versus real authority, and responding to Almudi, Fatas-Villafranca, Foster, and Potts (2024) on multi-population coevolutionary dynamics, the paper treats the protectorate as an interaction among three populations: mid-managers, operational interdependents, and enterprise governance. Operationally embedded coalitions, in the sense of Granovetter (1985), hold collectively non-contractible operational knowledge that no single agent can convey externally. Two results follow. First, the protectorate is structurally stable yet content-mutating: the layer reconstitutes after leadership turnover because encoded knowledge is non-substitutable, while routines mutate through coalition-driven adaptation in response to enterprise governance pressure, so what persists is a coalition-shaped variant rather than the original routine. Second, standard agency-cost mitigations designed for single-agent settings are structurally inadequate against operationally embedded coalitions because the mitigations target the wrong unit of analysis. The paper distinguishes the protectorate from street-level bureaucracy, organizational inertia, and standard micropolitics, and contributes a structural account of meso-layer institutional dynamics in matrixed multinationals. Operationally embedded coalitions in matrixed multinationals produce a structurally stable but content-mutating institutional layer, the protectorate, that defeats agency-cost mitigations designed for single-agent settings because the coalition holds collectively non-contractible information no individual agent can convey externally.

title: Crypto Regulation Shouldn't be Cryptic: The Continuing need for Legislative Clarification
affiliations: University of Arkansas, Fayetteville - School of Law

detail.title: Crypto Regulation Shouldn't be Cryptic: The Continuing need for Legislative Clarification
detail.abstract:
Prior to 2025, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) pursued a very active and aggressive enforcement agenda against crypto enterprises without adopting rules that explained when it would assert jurisdiction. At that time, there was mounting pressure on Congress to enact comprehensive crypto legislation to address what was widely seen as a lack of clarity and certainty as to the scope of federal securities laws as they apply to crypto assets.

Under leadership selected by President Trump, the rash of new enforcement actions from the SEC abruptly stopped. Ongoing investigations were halted, and most pending enforcement actions were dismissed, even those that were at the appellate stage. A new Crypto Task Force turned its attention to developing rules specifically focused on crypto assets. A new interpretive rule suggested a much more limited role for the agency when it comes to crypto assets.

Although this might suggest that there are no longer compelling reasons for legislative clarification, this Article suggests that the need for Congressional action is as great now as it was before the SEC’s enforcement push died down. Without legislative or judicial clarification, we cannot know the appropriate scope of the federal securities laws. Even though the SEC under President Trump is eschewing overly aggressive enforcement against most crypto businesses and attempting to adopt narrower interpretations of applicable statutes, there is no guarantee that this will continue in the future. And there is always the possibility that the courts will ultimately disagree with the agency’s new approach and interpretations. It is therefore important that Congress step in to provide the clarity and certainty that the crypto industry participants deserve.

title: Replicating Legacy is Squandering the Promise of Tokenisation: We Are Building a Faster Horse
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Former Head of Debt Capital Markets Trading at Fidelity International

detail.title: Replicating Legacy is Squandering the Promise of Tokenisation: We Are Building a Faster Horse
detail.abstract:
Blockchain, and the tokenisation that the technology enables, have the potential to create a new financial ecosystem, delivering compelling advantages to investors, and renewed competitiveness to the UK as a jurisdiction.

The paper explains why our current approach will fall well short of this potential – without higher ambition, we will only build a slightly faster horse, with no better outcomes, rather than a rapid, resilient and efficient vehicle. At best we will replicate our current financial ecosystem in a new technology. At worst, we will end up delivering no more than we can deliver now, but requiring two parallel technologies to deliver it.

If we allow this to be the outcome then, while there will be some benefits in speed and availability, these will often be outweighed by greater complexity and by the cost of maintaining two concurrent technologies.

This paper sets out the key attributes of an optimal, composable approach to tokenisation, and demonstrates how it can deliver strategic solutions to the systemic issues of investment.  It explains how the current game plan, promoted both by industry incumbents and by blockchain enthusiasts, can be valuable, but is the start-point, not the end-point; composability must be the target of digitisation.

We have the opportunity to set a new composable standard for global investment, to elevate what we deliver, and to expand our addressable market.  We know what will happen if we in the UK let the chance slip by: other jurisdictions will be only too happy to grab the initiative and exploit the opportunities that it brings.

Finally, the paper makes clear why embedding all the attributes of existing assets and products into tokens is counter-productive, and will hinder us in our efforts to realise the full potential of what we have started.  We have a rare opportunity: a fresh canvas to fix systemic inefficiencies and value extraction, before they become embedded in digital innovation. More importantly, we have the chance to broaden what financial services can deliver, and to whom, rather than concretising what we currently deliver in a new technology.

The call to action is very clear - we must deliver a composable financial ecosystem before someone else beats us to it, and we must resolve, rather than replicate, the deficiencies of our current financial services infrastructure.

title: Optimizing Network Security and Power Consumption: An Architectural Analysis of the PacketHawk Intrusion Detection Framework
affiliations: Vellore Institute of Technology, Vellore Institute of Technology, Vellore Institute of Technology and Vellore Institute of Technology

detail.title: Optimizing Network Security and Power Consumption: An Architectural Analysis of the PacketHawk Intrusion Detection Framework
detail.abstract: Nowadays the modern high-speed networks face two critical challenges, which are maintaining top level security, while at the same time reducing energy usage. As the data transmission rates grow as much as to petabyte rates, the computational expense of inspecting the network traffic has become a major issue in performance. The traditional network intrusion detection systems (IDS), which relies on signature matching, struggles to scale efficiently, which results in increased latency, reduced packet delivery ratio (PDR), and excessive power consumption. This paper illustrates a detailed evaluation of PacketHawk, a smart framework engineered to overcome the above limitations through the application of Decision Tree (DT) algorithm. This framework relies on foundational documentation and thorough research, including the studies by Jadhav et al. (2024) and Jiang et al. (2021), the work breaks down the system’s architecture logic and operating efficiency. this work experimental analysis using the NSL-KDD (Network Security Laboratory - Knowledge Discovery in Databases) dataset confirms that PacketHawk attains 100% detection accuracy, while only taking the processing latency of just 0.0006% ms per network packet. Besides, the work investigates the downstream effects of the ultra-low latency, highlighting its direct relation with enhanced quality of service (QoS), higher throughput, and reduction in footprint of network security operations.

detail.abstract: We study changes in profit inefficiency and propose decompositions that link this measure to changes in technical and allocative inefficiency via the duality between the profit function and existing measures of technical inefficiency. Methodologically, we show that the additive measurement of profit inefficiency critically depends on the values of the normalization factors obtained through the dual relationships. These normalization factors differ among observations and time periods hampering the contemporary (static) and temporal (dynamic) comparison of results between and within observations. To address this issue, we propose a decomposition of profit inefficiency change in monetary terms, obtained by multiplying each component of the decomposition by its corresponding normalization factor. Ultimately, only the decomposition of profit inefficiency based on the directional distance function can offer comparable results for all observations and time periods by ensuring common normalization factors that result in monetary valuations. The models are computationally implemented using Data Envelopment Analysis and new functions developed in the open-source Julia language, which are incorporated into the package 'BenchmarkingEconomicEfficiency.jl'. For completeness, we extend these functions to multiplicative definitions of changes in profitability, cost and revenue efficiency. The article details the theoretical methods and the empirical implementation of the functions using a common dataset on Taiwanese Banks.

title: The Da'wah Strategy of Prophet Muhammad ‫ﷺ‬ during the Makkan Period
affiliations: Superior University

detail.title: The Da'wah Strategy of Prophet Muhammad ‫ﷺ‬ during the Makkan Period
detail.abstract: The Makkan period of Prophet Muhammad's ‫ﷺ‬ mission represents one of the most significant phases in the history of Islamic da'wah. Spanning approximately thirteen years, this period (610 to 622 CE) was marked by ideological resistance, socio-political, psychological pressure, economic boycott, and physical persecution. Despite the absence of political power, military authority, or institutional support, the Prophet ‫ﷺ‬ succeeded in establishing a deeply rooted community based on tawḥīd, moral reform, intellectual awakening, patience, and spiritual discipline. The strategic depth of the Makkan period is further illuminated through the lens of critical historiography, which weighs traditional narratives. This article critically examines the da'wah strategy of the Prophet ‫ﷺ‬ during the Makkan period, highlighting its gradual nature, ethical foundation, psychological depth, social inclusiveness, and long-term transformative vision. Each major point is followed by a critical and logical viewpoint to demonstrate how the Prophetic method was not merely religious preaching but a comprehensive strategy for human, moral, and social reconstruction.

title: Trust in Human–Artificial Intelligence Interactions
affiliations: University of Toronto

detail.title: Trust in Human–Artificial Intelligence Interactions
detail.abstract: As AI systems take on consequential public roles, building trust in human–machine interaction has become central to responsible deployment. This paper examines how trust in AI is understood across technical, social science, and humanities disciplines, identifying six shaping principles: reliability and competence; contextual awareness; transparency, accountability, and legitimacy; fairness and integrity; resilience; and relational dynamics. These principles reveal that trust in AI is not a fixed attitude or technical property, but an ongoing relational process linking system performance to social legitimacy. A sociotechnical framework, combining functional reliability with social value alignment, is necessary to ground trust in justified confidence rather than institutional pressure or automation bias. Ultimately, developing trustworthy AI is a multidisciplinary endeavor. The defining question is not only whether AI systems perform well, but whether they are governed in ways that societies can legitimately rely on.

detail.abstract: In the 21st century, the strategic integration of business objectives and information technology (IT) has become fundamental drivers of organizational competitiveness, innovation, and sustainability. Advancements in digital technologies—such as cloud computing, data analytics, artificial intelligence, and enterprise information systems—have transformed traditional business models and redefined the role of IT from an operational support function to a strategic enabler. The alignment between business strategy and IT strategy is essential, as emphasized by various frameworks, including competitive strategies and the value chain model. These frameworks highlight how technology can support cost leadership, differentiation, and market focus while optimizing key business activities. Despite its benefits, the integration of IT into business strategy presents challenges such as cybersecurity risks, rapid technological change, and skills shortages. Nevertheless, organizations that strategically adopt and manage IT are better positioned to thrive in a dynamic and globalized environment. Ultimately, IT is not merely a tool but a central component of strategic planning and long-term business success in the digital age. This paper examines the evolving relationship between strategic business management and information technology, emphasizing business–IT alignment, digital transformation, governance, and IT-enabled competitive advantage.

title: Why HR Often Fails the Employee Experience: A Critical Analysis of Trust, Role Conflict, and the Limits of Transactional Human Resource Design
affiliations: Mindanao State University - Iligan Institute of Technology

detail.title: Why HR Often Fails the Employee Experience: A Critical Analysis of Trust, Role Conflict, and the Limits of Transactional Human Resource Design
detail.abstract: This paper examines why human resource (HR) departments often fail to meet employee expectations despite being positioned as central to employee experience, trust, and organizational support. It argues that the problem is not simply poor HR execution, but a deeper structural contradiction: organizations expect HR to be both employee-centered and administratively efficient while resourcing it primarily as a transactional control function. It aims to reframe employee dissatisfaction with HR as an organizational design problem rather than a narrow service-quality issue. The paper uses a critical practitioner-oriented analysis of a Wall Street Journal article discussing the mismatch between employee expectations and HR performance. Drawing on psychological contract theory, HR system strength, and strategic human resource management, it interprets the article through an organizational design lens. The approach is conceptual and analytical rather than empirical, using the article as a trigger for broader managerial reflection on trust, role conflict, automation, and the operating logic of HR in contemporary organizations. The analysis finds that employee disappointment with HR stems from three interrelated problems: inflated psychological expectations, unresolved role conflict, and weak operating-model design. HR is often expected to deliver empathy, development, and trust while also enforcing policy, managing compliance, and protecting organizational interests. Automation can reduce friction in routine transactions, but it does not automatically build legitimacy or trust. The paper concludes that stronger HR performance depends on clearer role definition, better escalation structures, coherent service design, and realistic organizational promises about what HR can and cannot deliver. This paper adds value by moving beyond the common view that HR underperforms because it is too bureaucratic or insufficiently empathetic. Instead, it shows that dissatisfaction with HR is rooted in a structural mismatch between symbolic expectations and institutional design. Its originality lies in treating HR not merely as a support function but as a governance interface through which the psychological contract is tested. The paper 2 offers a sharper conceptual basis for managers seeking to redesign HR around legitimacy, coherence, and trust rather than around administrative efficiency alone.

title: A Hybrid AE–WGAN–HCBOU Framework for Rare Attack Augmentation and Class-Imbalanced Intrusion Detection
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Concordia University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Concordia University

detail.title: A Hybrid AE–WGAN–HCBOU Framework for Rare Attack Augmentation and Class-Imbalanced Intrusion Detection
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital infrastructures and the increasing sophistication of cyberattacks have made Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) a critical component of modern network security. A major challenge in this domain is the extreme imbalance among attack classes in real-world datasets, where critical attack categories often constitute less than 10\% of total traffic. This imbalance leads to poor detection performance for rare attacks, as machine learning and deep learning models are biased toward majority classes. Traditional oversampling methods fail to capture the complex non-linear structure of minority distributions, while classical generative models suffer from instability and mode collapse when trained on sparse data. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel Hierarchical Cluster-Based Over- and Under-Sampling (HCBOU) mechanism that performs distribution-aware allocation of synthetic samples in latent space, ensuring balanced coverage across fragmented minority-class regions. Unlike existing approaches that focus solely on generating synthetic data, the proposed method explicitly controls where synthetic samples are placed, thereby preserving the intrinsic structure of the minority manifold. To support this, an autoencoder is employed to learn a compact and noise-reduced latent representation, and a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) is used to generate stable and diverse synthetic samples. HCBOU then enforces cluster-level density balancing, preventing oversampling in dense regions and improving representation in sparse regions. The proposed framework is evaluated on three benchmark intrusion detection datasets using multiple classifier backbones. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in recall and F1-score for rare attack classes, highlighting the effectiveness of distribution-aware augmentation over traditional oversampling and standard GAN-based methods.

title: How Big Data Analytics Capability Affects Digital Servitization: Considering the Mediating Effect of Digital Innovation and the Moderating Effect of Environmental Uncertainty
affiliations: Hefei University of Technology, Hefei University of Technology and Hefei University of Technology

detail.title: How Big Data Analytics Capability Affects Digital Servitization: Considering the Mediating Effect of Digital Innovation and the Moderating Effect of Environmental Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Drawing a capability-building perspective, this study examines how big data analytics capability, a lower-order functional capability, shapes digital innovation, a higher-order dynamic capability, and thereby facilitates digital servitization. We further investigate how environmental uncertainty conditions the effect of digital innovation on digital servitization. Using data from 160 matched-pair questionnaires combined with objective environmental data from China, we find that data-driven decision culture, big data technical skills, and big data managerial skills all foster digital innovation, which in turn promotes digital servitization. We also find that environmental dynamism and environmental complexity positively moderate the relationship between digital innovation and digital servitization. This study contributes to the literature by clarifying the links among big data analytics capability, digital innovation, and digital servitization, and by showing how these relationships vary across environmental conditions. Practically, our findings suggest that managers should strengthen big data analytics capability and digital innovation to advance digital servitization, while remaining attentive to environmental changes.

reference: Politics, Philosophy & Economics, 0[10.1177/1470594X261450600]; Politics, Philosophy & Economics (forthcoming)
title: Are Markets Coercive?
affiliations: University of San Diego

detail.title: Are Markets Coercive?
detail.abstract: Are markets coercive? Contemporary debate is dominated by two answers. The first, longstanding among defenders of free markets, holds that voluntary exchange is noncoercive by definition: coercion enters the picture only when rights are violated. The second, revived from Robert Hale's 1923 essay and embraced today by progressive legal scholars and post-liberal conservatives alike, holds that markets are pervasively coercive because property rights backed by state power constitute a system of mutual coercion. Both answers fail, but the Halean answer fails in the more interesting way. The libertarian answer moralizes coercion, stripping it of evaluative force; the Halean answer demoralizes coercion, stripping it of discriminating power. If coercion is everywhere, it cannot pick out the arrangements worth criticizing. Drawing on a convergence across the philosophical literature on coercion, the paper develops a third option: identify coercion non-moralistically-as a factual matter of options restricted by another's institutionally backed power-but evaluate its significance in graduated terms, by attention to the significance of the options curtailed, the availability of alternatives, and the directness of compulsion involved. The result is a framework that can distinguish cases of genuinely worrisome market coercion from cases where the concept does no moral work.

title: Urban Ecosystem Services in Decline: The Environmental Cost of Urban Expansion in U.S. Metropolitan Areas From 2001 To 2021
affiliations: University of Minnesota, University of Minnesota, University of Minnesota - St. Paul - Institute on the Environment, University of Minnesota - Twin Cities, Emory University, NatCap Insights and University of Minnesota, Twin Cities - Department of Applied Economics

detail.title: Urban Ecosystem Services in Decline: The Environmental Cost of Urban Expansion in U.S. Metropolitan Areas From 2001 To 2021

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There are no financial or personal relationships, activities, or patents to disclose.
declarations.funderStatement: This material is based upon work supported by the U.S. Geological Survey under Grant No. G23AC00663-00.

detail.abstract: We quantify access to green space and the monetary ecosystem service values for urban cooling, stormwater retention, and carbon storage for 380 metropolitan areas in the contiguous U.S. in 2001, 2011, and 2021, using the Urban Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs (Urban InVEST) software. We find significant values of ecosystem services in urban areas, $1.5 billion in urban cooling from reduced energy expenditures, $20.3 billion in reduced stormwater retention costs, and $24.6 billion in the annual rental value of carbon storage in 2021. However, we find decreases in the provision of ecosystem services over the 20-year period across most metropolitan areas, reflecting a loss of urban green space. The rate of loss has slowed over time with greater losses from 2001 to 2011 than from 2011 to 2021.

title: HOUSEHOLD COOLING CHOICES UNDER HEAT STRESS AND,ENERGY CONSTRAINTS IN CENTRAL ASIA
affiliations: OSCE Academy, Asian Development Bank, Independent and NUPI - Norwegian Institute of International Affairs

detail.title: HOUSEHOLD COOLING CHOICES UNDER HEAT STRESS AND,ENERGY CONSTRAINTS IN CENTRAL ASIA
detail.abstract: This study investigates the factors influencing household cooling choices in Central Asia, using data from the survey ”Household Access to Energy in the Fergana Valley”, conducted in Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan in 2023. The study examines the adoption of air conditioning, fans, and sunscreen films as cooling solutions. Using a multinomial probit model, the analysis reveals that adoption of air conditioning is strongly influenced by household income, the education level of heads of households, urban residency, reliability of electricity supply and the heat level of the household’s location. Fans and sunscreen films are more commonly adopted by larger households and those in regions with extreme heat. Further robust analysis incorporating the duration of power outages demonstrates that households in areas with frequent or prolonged disruptions are less likely to adopt energy-intensive cooling technologies such as air conditioning. Fans and sunscreen films are more feasible options in such areas, since they require less energy and are more resilient to power supply interruptions. The study also highlights the significant role of climatic conditions, particularly cooling degree days, in shaping household cooling preferences.

title: Cultural Additivity Theory
affiliations: Vietnam National University (VNU) and Phenikaa University

detail.title: Cultural Additivity Theory
detail.abstract: This paper presents Cultural Additivity Theory (CAT) as a process framework for explaining how cultural systems interact, absorb, transform, and recombine information-value bundles. While the term cultural additivity was pioneered by Vuong et al. (2018) to analyze the syncretic nature of Vietnamese folktales, it has not yet been elaborated as a general theory of cultural interaction. This study addresses that gap by defining CAT as a continuous process in which agents, situated in natural and social environments, process information-value bundles in pursuit of survival and sustainable development. CAT is articulated through four core components, a three-level hierarchy of interaction (exchange, compatibility, and resonance), and a value-comparison formula that admits linear, super-additive, and sub-additive outcomes. The theory further identifies three erosive mechanisms: conflict-driven destruction, high-entropy capacity strain, and low-entropy structural lock-in. By examining theory-illustrating cases ranging from funeral rites to the highadditivity paradox of Vietnamese culture, the paper shows how CAT can function both as an analytical lens and as a generator of empirically testable hypotheses for studying cultural resilience, innovation, and erosion in the modern world.

title: DEF-Net: Detection-oriented Enhancement–Discriminative Feature Underwater Detection Network
affiliations: Harbin Engineering University, Harbin Engineering University, Harbin Engineering University, Shandong University of Science and Technology, Harbin Engineering University, Harbin Engineering University and Harbin Engineering University

detail.title: DEF-Net: Detection-oriented Enhancement–Discriminative Feature Underwater Detection Network

keywords.keywords: Underwater Object Detection (UOD)  Degradation-Aware Enhancement Spatial-Frequency RepresentationRobust Feature Learning

detail.abstract: ​  Underwater object detection is chronically hindered by light absorption, scattering, and blurring, which compromise the integrity of high-frequency structural cues. While conventional enhancement methods improve human-centric visual fidelity, they frequently overlook task-specific alignment, inadvertently introducing detrimental feature distribution shifts and semantic noise. In this paper, we propose DEF-Net,a detection-oriented Enhancement–discriminative Feature Network for underwater object detection that achieves synergistic collaboration between image restoration and discriminative feature modeling without relying on unstable multi-task joint optimization.   Specifically, we first introduce the Degradation-Driven Detection-Friendly Enhancement (D³FE) module, which performs conservative, degradation-aware restoration at the input level to stabilize the data distribution while safeguarding critical structural primitives. To mitigate enhancement-induced perturbations, the HeteroFlow-DynamicNet (HF-DN) is employed to conduct dynamic multi-scale spatial–frequency collaborative modeling, effectively decoupling noise from semantic features to reinforce discriminative power. Finally, a Density-Guided Feature Enhancement (DGFE) module provides targeted compensation for small and densely distributed objects that remain vulnerable post-restoration. By reorganizing features to selectively absorb task-relevant gains while neutralizing noise propagation, DEF-Net ensures robust feature constancy across diverse underwater environments. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that DEF-Net consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance, exhibiting superior generalization and structural integrity under complex underwater degradations.

title: Novel Multi-Parameter Identification Method for High-Speed Railway Subgrade Settlement: A Strategy Based on Physical Prior Modulation Fusion
affiliations: Beijing Jiaotong University, Beijing Jiaotong University, Beijing Jiaotong University, Beijing Jiaotong University and Beijing Jiaotong University

detail.title: Novel Multi-Parameter Identification Method for High-Speed Railway Subgrade Settlement: A Strategy Based on Physical Prior Modulation Fusion
detail.abstract: Subgrade differential settlement can compromise ride safety and operational stability by intensifying wheel–rail interaction and vehicle–track vibrations. Early-grade identification remains challenging due to weak onset response variations and the nonstationarity of acceleration signals. Conventional data-driven models often provide neither physics-consistent indicators nor well-calibrated confidence for threshold-based alarms and risk grading. Physics-Aware Time-Series Mixer with feature-wise linear modulation priors (PATS) is developed for ordinal identification of settlement amplitude A, wavelength L, and lateral coefficient K using carbody lateral and vertical accelerations. PATS integrates (1) improved complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (ICEEMDAN) to separate low-frequency geometric trends from mid-to-high-frequency impacts, (2) physics-informed descriptors, namely sensitive intrinsic mode function (IMF) energy priors and statistics-based cumulative characteristic function (SCCF) features, injected into a lightweight Time-Series Mixer (TSMixer) backbone via feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), and (3) a multi-group ordinal head based on consistent rank logits (CORAL) to output reliability-aware probabilities. Experiments show 97.41% accuracy with 0.0187 expected calibration error (ECE) on K at 1.050 ms/sample, 96.30% accuracy with 0.0350 ECE on A at 0.964 ms/sample, and 100.00% accuracy with 0.0011 ECE on L. The artificial intelligence contribution lies in an interpretable physics-guided prior injection mechanism for nonstationary multivariate time-series grading, coupled with a reliability-oriented ordinal output design. The engineering application contribution is a deployable onboard monitoring framework for early-grade identification of high-speed railway subgrade differential settlement from onboard accelerations, enabling threshold-based alarming and risk grading.

title: An Economic Theory of “Two Fears” in Corporate Governance: Shareholder Heterogeneity and Market Pressures
affiliations: Kansas State University - Department of Economics

detail.title: An Economic Theory of “Two Fears” in Corporate Governance: Shareholder Heterogeneity and Market Pressures
detail.abstract: This paper presents a game-theoretic analysis of the internal and external pressures that shape a firm's operational objectives, which we refer to as the “two fears” in corporate governance. The first fear arises internally from diverse shareholder interests, while the second fear comes externally from competition with profit-maximizing rivals. In contrast to the outcomes associated with profit maximization in a standard Cournot oligopoly, our analysis through a two-stage game shows that a firm’s operational objectives—focused on maximizing firm profits and consumer utility—result in a profit-shifting effect. This strategy, aimed at maximizing a combined profit-cum-utility objective function, results in a win-win equilibrium for all diverse shareholders. In this scenario, a firm’s profits increase while competitors’ profits decrease. However, the profit-shifting effect and the win-win equilibrium do not manifest in a monopoly. All shareholders must agree that profit maximization is the monopoly's primary objective. This finding aligns with the traditional doctrine of profit maximization. In the context of oligopolistic competition, we demonstrate that the two fears in corporate governance highlight the importance of integrating shareholder heterogeneity with market pressures when establishing a firm's operational objectives. This study has significant implications for the relationship between shareholders and stakeholders (such as consumers).

title: A multi-label supervised contrastive loss with continuous positiveness
affiliations: Sabanci University, Sabanci University, University of Lincoln and Maastricht University

detail.title: A multi-label supervised contrastive loss with continuous positiveness
detail.abstract: Multi-Label scene classification constitutes a fundamental task in remote sensing, as it addresses real-world complexity by enabling a sample to have multiple land-cover categories. In this context, supervised contrastive learning is one of the prominent frameworks of multi-label multi-class classification. However, existing variants impose a discrete positiveness among samples (i.e.~a sample is either positive or not w.r.t~the anchor). We propose a new supervised multi-label contrastive loss that addresses this limitation via a continuous positiveness representation. The proposed method learns more discriminative representations than the standard binary paradigm by weighing contrastive forces based on label similarity. Experiments conducted across three optical remote sensing datasets indicate that the proposed strategy outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods with a significant margin.

title: Multi-spectral solar active region detection via cross-attention fusion in yolov10
affiliations: Kim Il Sung University, Kim Il Sung University, Kim Il Sung University, Kim Il Sung University and Kim Il Sung University

detail.title: Multi-spectral solar active region detection via cross-attention fusion in yolov10
detail.abstract: Monitoring solar active regions (ARs) is essential for space weather forecasting, satellite operations, and astronaut safety. While deep learning has advanced AR detection, existing methods typically rely on single-wavelength images, missing complementary information across the electromagnetic spectrum. This paper presents MS-YOLOv10, a novel multi-spectral object detection framework that fuses Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (HMI) continuum images with Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) 211 Å and 335 Å channels. Unlike prior fusion approaches using simple concatenation or attention modules, we introduce a Cross-Attention Fusion Module (CAFM) that dynamically aligns and integrates features from different wavelengths before the backbone, plus a Multi-Scale Feature Refinement (MSFR) block in the neck. Trained on a newly constructed dataset of 15,000 aligned triple-band images (2010–2024), our method achieves mAP@0.5=0.96 and mAP@0.5:0.95=0.61, outperforming single-wavelength baselines by 4–7% and prior fusion methods (CatFuse, CBAMC, TransEnc) by 2–12%. Statistical analysis via Friedman test (p<0.001) and Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests confirms significance. Ablation studies reveal that cross-attention fusion at the backbone input is critical, and that temporal context further improves performance. Our code and dataset are publicly available.

title: CurioTrojan: A Curiosity-driven Spatiotemporal Backdoor Attack against Competitive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
affiliations: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Wuhan University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

detail.title: CurioTrojan: A Curiosity-driven Spatiotemporal Backdoor Attack against Competitive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
detail.abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) integrates the perceptual capabilities of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) with the decision-making abilities of Reinforcement Learning (RL), enabling broad applications. However, recent studies reveal that DRL inevitably faces the threat of backdoor attacks. Such attacks embed hidden triggers into DRL models during training, causing models to perform normally under clean environments while executing malicious behaviors upon encountering specific triggers. Existing backdoor attacks against DRL predominantly inherit supervised learning paradigms, relying on handcrafted, instantaneous triggers that activate attacks immediately upon presentation. This paradigm is fundamentally at odds with the sequential decision-making nature of DRL, often leading to detectable behavioral anomalies. To this end, we propose a curiosity-driven spatiotemporal trigger mining mechanism, CurioTrojan, for automated backdoor construction in competitive multi-agent systems. Leveraging random network distillation to implement the curiosity mechanism, CurioTrojan quantifies a victim agent's familiarity with environmental states, autonomously exploring rare observation sequences to generate stealthy triggers. The attacker agent strategically manipulates its behavior to induce these trigger conditions in the victim's observations, thereby activating latent backdoors that subvert the victim's competitive performance. Experimental results demonstrate that our CurioTrojan can achieve stealthy backdoor attacks, which can obtain a 90.2% attack success rate, maintain a clean performance deviation (0.1%), and effectively evade detection by advanced backdoor defenses.

title: Operationalizing Transaction Cost Economics for Contract Governance: Evidence from Procurement Data
affiliations: Air Force Institute of Technology and Air Force Institute of Technology

detail.title: Operationalizing Transaction Cost Economics for Contract Governance: Evidence from Procurement Data
detail.abstract: Selecting an appropriate contract type is a central decision in purchasing and supply management, shaping incentives, risk allocation, and buyer–supplier relationships. Drawing on Transaction Cost Economics (TCE), this study examines how observable procurement characteristics can inform contract governance choice. Using a dataset of over 2,500 U.S. federal service contracts, we develop and test empirical models that relate contract attributes—such as competition structure, subcontracting, performance specifications, and contract value—to governance form (fixed price versus cost plus), providing a large-scale empirical setting with broader implications for procurement and supply chain governance. Our results provide large-sample evidence that commonly available procurement data serve as meaningful proxies for transaction cost dimensions, including asset specificity and complexity. Several contract features are significantly associated with governance choice, supporting TCE predictions, while interaction effects reveal more nuanced relationships. In particular, the findings suggest that asset specificity moderates the influence of complexity on governance selection, highlighting conditional effects that extend prior empirical applications of TCE. Building on these insights, we develop predictive models that use only information available at the time of contract design. These models improve contract-type classification accuracy by approximately 14 percent relative to an informed baseline, demonstrating practical value for procurement decision-making. Overall, the study advances purchasing and supply management research by operationalizing TCE with observable data, offering empirically grounded guidance for contract design, and bridging theory and empirically grounded decision-support approaches for contract design.

title: Quantifying Investor-Driven Overvaluation in the Australian Housing Market: An Empirical Demand Attribution Price Model

detail.title: Quantifying Investor-Driven Overvaluation in the Australian Housing Market: An Empirical Demand Attribution Price Model
detail.abstract: This paper presents an empirical demand-pressure price model to calculate overvaluation of the Australian established housing market sector from 1999 to the present, a period marked by sustained investor demand supported by three generous tax concessions. The price model is intrinsically expressed in the economic fundamental: in a supply limited market demand drives prices up, housing buyer and price data allow market specific implementation of the model and in Australia’s case established housing supply is essentially fixed. Furthermore, buyers account for economic factors in their decision to buy or not along with the bank’s decision on lending to buyers. The model attributes marginal real house price movements to buyer types: first home buyers, non first home buyer owner-occupiers and investors. By tracking relative demand-pressure shifts of each buyer type with corresponding price changes, the model attributes the proportion of price inflation driven by buyer type.While all buyer type demand contributes to house price inflation, only the investorattributable portion is treated as overvaluation, as it is driven primarily by tax distortions and expectations of future capital gains rather than housing consumption needs. This direct approach analysis indicates that approximately 46% of real house prices at the end of 2024 was attributable to investor-induced demand which equates to an 84% overvaluation of the established housing market. The evolution of this overvaluation meets Nobel Laureate Joseph Stiglitz’s definition of an asset bubble with one caveat, it is a rational bubble so long as investors believe the tax concessions will remain in place for the long term, a belief grounded not in economics but in historical political mandate. Notably, since the second tax concession investors own or have owned and traded approximately 9.6 million homes, a number representing 90% of Australia’s 11 million dwellings, illustrating the unprecedented scale of investor dominance in the Australian housing market.

title: A Constraint-Aware Benchmark for Evaluating Data Augmentation in Binary Strabismus Detection
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Constraint-Aware Benchmark for Evaluating Data Augmentation in Binary Strabismus Detection
detail.abstract: Background and Objective:Data augmentation is a prevalent technique in deep learning for medical image analysis, aimed at enhancing generalisation when labelled data are scarce. However, its true impact in resource-limited clinical settings is not yet clear. This study investigates binary strabismus referral classification for esotropia and exotropia using lightweight convolutional neural networks, specifically EfficientNet-B0, MobileNet-V2, and MobileNet-V3. We introduce a constraint-aware benchmarking framework to systematically evaluate whether data augmentation consistently improves upon baseline models across datasets, architectures, and evaluation metrics.Methods:We propose UBAEF, a constraint-aware benchmarking framework designed to evaluate multiple data augmentation strategies under conservative training conditions. Two datasets representing esotropia and exotropia are treated as distinct binary classification tasks. The aforementioned lightweight CNN architectures are employed, with six augmentation strategies compared against a non-augmented baseline. All models are trained under identical pipelines to ensure fair comparisons, with performance metrics including accuracy, specificity, precision, negative predictive value, and Brier score, particularly focusing on calibration through decomposition. Statistical significance of results is assessed using the DeLong test and the McNemar test.Results:Overall, data augmentation did not consistently exceed baseline performance across models. In several instances, augmented models exhibited slight declines in accuracy, specificity, precision, and negative predictive value, while baseline models remained competitive. Dataset-specific analyses revealed that AutoAugment and TrivialAugment occasionally enhanced performance in esotropia, whereas CutMix underperformed. In the exotropia dataset, TrivialAugment proved to be relatively stable. Variation in model performance indicated that augmentation effects were architecture dependent. Statistical assessments using the DeLong and McNemar tests revealed no consistent significant improvements. Calibration analysis indicated that Mixup achieved the highest reliability and AutoAugment demonstrated the strongest resolution, though these effects were inconsistent across conditions.Conclusions:This study presents a benchmarking framework addressing constraints for evaluating data augmentation in binary strabismus referral classification, especially in low-resource settings. The investigated augmentation methods did not consistently enhance performance compared to baseline models and often resulted in slight performance degradation. Their efficacy varied by dataset and architecture, underscoring the importance of context. Hence, selective use of data augmentation is advised in clinical environments, with AutoAugment being seen as the most consistent for constrained settings.

title: Choosing between CNN and Transformer for coronary CTA stenosis grading: A systematic comparison across 18 architectures
affiliations: Hebei University, Hebei University, Hebei University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Hebei University

detail.title: Choosing between CNN and Transformer for coronary CTA stenosis grading: A systematic comparison across 18 architectures
detail.abstract: Objective: To systematically benchmark 18 deep learning architectures for five-class coronary artery stenosis grading on CTA curved planar reformation (CPR) images, encompassing CNNs, lightweight networks,  Vision Transformer (ViT) and Swin Transformer.Methods: We retrospectively collected 5,078 CPR images from the Affiliated Hospital of Hebei University (2,337 nonstenotic, 588 mild (1-24%), 955 mild (25-49%), 460 moderate (50-69%), and 738 severe (≥70%)). The mild (1-24%), moderate, and severe categories were doubled by 90°rotation, resulting in 6,864 images. All images were center-cropped and resized to 224×224 pixels. A total of 18 representative deep learning architectures were selected for benchmarking, spanning classic CNNs (e.g., GoogLeNet, ResNet, DenseNet), lightweight networks (e.g., MobileNet, ShuffleNet, MobileViT), and Vision Transformers (ViT, Swin Transformer). All models were uniformly trained from scratch using the cross-entropy loss function to ensure a fair comparison under limited medical data conditions.Results: EfficientNetV2 achieved the highest accuracy (85.86%) and weighted Kappa (0.7877). ResNeXt101 (83.56%), EfficientNet (83.16%), and ResNet50 (82.91%) also performed well. MobileViT reached 81.85% accuracy with 0.95 M parameters and 0.81 ms inference time, representing an optimal efficiency-accuracy trade-off suitable for edge deployment. ViT (61.37%) and Swin Transformer (62.83%) significantly underperformed CNNs, likely due to the lack of pre-training. Moderate stenosis (50–69%) yielded the lowest F1 score (77.27%) across all models.Conclusions: This study provides a quantitative benchmark for AI-assisted coronary stenosis grading. EfficientNetV2 is recommended when accuracy is the priority. MobileViT and ShuffleNet offer good accuracyefficiency tradeoffs for resourcelimited settings. This study provides a benchmark for model selection in AIassisted coronary stenosis grading.

title: Are Day-of-the-Week Effects in Cryptocurrencies Real?  Intraday Evidence from Active and Less Active Cryptocurrencies​
affiliations: University of Rhode Island - Area of Finance and Insurance, University of Michigan at Flint and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Are Day-of-the-Week Effects in Cryptocurrencies Real?  Intraday Evidence from Active and Less Active Cryptocurrencies​
detail.abstract: This study revisits calendar anomalies in cryptocurrency markets using hourly data for four actively traded cryptocurrencies (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tether USDt, and BNB) and eight less active cryptocurrencies. While prior studies based on daily returns provide mixed evidence on day-of-the-week (DoW) effects, we show that these patterns are not persistent daily phenomena. Instead, they are driven by a limited number of intraday intervals and do not reflect broad daily behavior.We further document that these effects are localized, asset-specific, and more pronounced among actively traded cryptocurrencies, while largely absent among less active ones.Overall, the findings indicate that cryptocurrency markets exhibit limited and short-lived inefficiencies rather than persistent anomalies. This highlights the importance of employing high-frequency data in studies of continuously traded markets and suggests that digital asset investors may benefit from the presence of abnormal returns only in a limited number of hours on specific days of the week.

title: Technology, Talent, and High-Quality Development in China: Time-Varying Evidence on Macroeconomic Resilience
affiliations: Changchun University of Technology and Changchun University of Technology

detail.title: Technology, Talent, and High-Quality Development in China: Time-Varying Evidence on Macroeconomic Resilience
detail.abstract: As China moves from factor-driven expansion toward high-quality development, a key question is how technological change can be translated into sustained productivity growth and macroeconomic resilience. This paper investigates how technology- and talent-related factors jointly shape high-quality development in China. Using quarterly macroeconomic data from 2007Q1 to 2024Q4, this study combines a stochastic-volatility time-varying-parameter factor-augmented vector autoregression (SV-TVP-FAVAR) model with a Markov-switching autoregressive (MS-AR) framework to identify their time-varying effects on total factor productivity and macroeconomic regime transitions. The results show that technological factors generate a faster and stronger short-run impulse, whereas talent factors play a slower but more persistent stabilising role. Neither factor alone is sufficient to support durable high-quality development: technological upgrading without effective talent absorption produces limited long-run gains, while talent accumulation without continued technological transformation has weaker productivity effects. By contrast, their joint effect more effectively supports transitions from lower-growth to higher-growth regimes and helps sustain macroeconomic stability. These findings suggest that the developmental value of technological change depends not only on innovation input, but also on talent formation, policy coordination, and the institutional capacity to convert technological advances into productive outcomes.

title: JUE Insight: The Effect of 2012-2021 Building Code Revisions on Break-Even Rents of 3-story Apartments
affiliations: Purdue University - Department of Economics, and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: JUE Insight: The Effect of 2012-2021 Building Code Revisions on Break-Even Rents of 3-story Apartments
detail.abstract: Building codes establish minimum construction standards for new multifamily housing, yet their cumulative implications for rental affordability remain poorly understood. Between 2012 and 2021, the International Code Council adopted 130 revisions to the International Building Code affecting multifamily development. Using a detailed prototype of a three-story apartment building and holding material prices and labor productivity constant at 2024 levels, we find that 16 of these revisions raised national average construction costs by 9.9 percent relative to a 2009 baseline, with fire protection requirements accounting for 67 percent of the dollar-weighted increase. Translating these costs into break-even rents using local land prices and capitalization rates, the implied increase in monthly rent for a two-bedroom unit ranges from $134 to $222 across the most populous cities in each state, equivalent to an additional 3.4 percentage points of median renter income at the national average. The affordability burden falls disproportionately on renters in lower-income non-coastal markets, where the ratio of regulatory cost to baseline development cost is highest.

title: Opportunity Zones and the Housing Supply
affiliations: University of South Carolina

detail.title: Opportunity Zones and the Housing Supply
detail.abstract: I study whether the Opportunity Zones (OZ) program, one of the largest place-based development subsidies in U.S. history, generated new housing or merely reallocated development. Using a quarterly panel of residential address counts for all U.S. Census tracts from 2012 to 2025, I document that OZ designation displaced residential development from nearby tracts: non-OZ tracts within ten miles of a designated zone experienced a decline in address growth that mirrors the measured gain inside OZ boundaries, consistent with developers relocating projects across tract lines to capture the tax benefit rather than initiating new ones. Apparent housing gains inside designated tracts are fully attributable to development displaced from nearby communities. Formal tests of the combined effect fail to reject zero at conventional significance levels, casting doubt on the efficacy of the proposed expansion of OZ-style incentives in theOne Big Beautiful Bill Act for stimulating housing production absent complementary zoning or infrastructure reform.

title: A Study on the Estimation of Green Production Efficiency in Larimichthys Crocea Aquaculture and Its Influencing Factors
affiliations: Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University, Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University and Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University

detail.title: A Study on the Estimation of Green Production Efficiency in Larimichthys Crocea Aquaculture and Its Influencing Factors
detail.abstract: The larimichthys crocea is one of the most important commercially farmed marine fish species along China’s southeastern coast. Although the green transition of aquaculture has begun to show results at the macro level, there has been a lack of systematic assessment of green production efficiency at the micro level of individual farmers. Based on micro-level survey data from 117 aquaculture farmers in the main larimichthys crocea production areas of Fujian Province, this study employs an SBM-DEA model incorporating unplanned outputs to measure the industry’s green production efficiency and uses a Tobit regression model to identify its key influencing factors. The results indicate: (1) The average green production efficiency of aquaculture farmers is 0.681, with only 18.80% reaching the efficiency frontier, indicating significant variation among individuals; (2) The average scale efficiency was only 0.619, with 85.47% of the samples in the stage of increasing returns to scale; insufficient scale was the primary source of efficiency loss, and efficiency gains were concentrated in the transition from small to medium scale; (3) The efficiency difference between the traditional and ecological models did not pass the 5% significance test, and the independent driving effect of the technical model was not yet significant during the facility renovation transition period; (4) Educational attainment and farming experience have significant negative effects on efficiency, with marginal effects of -0.064 and -0.006, respectively; path dependence and the level of focus in part-time, decentralized management are possible underlying mechanisms. The study indicates that scale thresholds and human capital lock-in effects are the primary obstacles currently constraining the improvement of green production efficiency in the larimichthys crocea industry.
