title: Behavioral Macroeconomics, Kaleckian Post-Keynesian Economics, and Stratification Economics: Incorporating Social Identity
affiliations: Marquette University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Behavioral Macroeconomics, Kaleckian Post-Keynesian Economics, and Stratification Economics: Incorporating Social Identity
detail.abstract: Behavioral Macroeconomics draws on cognitive psychology's errors and biases approach to argue that psychological factors acting on individual choice affect how the economy functions. Keynes drew on psychology in his 'beauty contest' account of convention to explain individual investor expectations in terms of the average expectation of all investors. This assumes individual investors identify with the group of all investors, anticipating social psychology social identity analysis. Kaleckian Post-Keynesian Economics focuses on distributional conflict between capital and labor. This also assumes individual capitalists and laborers identify with groups of capitalists and laborers. Stratification Economics makes social group identity the basis on which economies operate as systems of intergroup inequalities. This raises two related questions: what role do economic agents' perceptions of their social identities have in explaining economies, and what does this imply for the Keynesian understanding of the income determination process and economic policy recommendation? This chapter discusses how social identity is understood in Stratification Economics to answer these questions.

title: Analysing the Legal and Policy Implications of the Investment and Securities Act 2025 on Digital Assets Offering Platforms

detail.title: Analysing the Legal and Policy Implications of the Investment and Securities Act 2025 on Digital Assets Offering Platforms
detail.abstract:
On 31st March, 2025, the Nigerian government signed into law the Investments and Securities Act (ISA) 2025, officially recognizing digital assets as securities. The Act repealed the Investment and Securities Act of 2007 (“ISA 2007”) to introduce transformative provisions to further align Nigeria’s market operations with global standards and reflect the changing investment landscape, including the evolvement of digital assets over the years, and other financial investment technologies.

This research analysed the legal implications of the innovative provisions of the Investment and Securities Act 2025 on Digital Assets Offering Platforms by examining key statutory provisions as they relate to the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020, the Investment and Securities Act, 2025, the Securities and Exchange Commission (Capital Market Operators Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism) Regulations, 2022, the Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance (NCCG) 2018 issued by the Financial Reporting Council of Nigeria and the Securities and Exchange Commission’ Corporate Governance Guidelines (SCGG). The analysis unravelled the key challenges faced by Digital Assets Offering Platforms seeking to comply with the applicable statutory provisions, ranging from Certain Anonymity-Enhanced Cryptocurrencies (AECs), conspiracy between Principal Officers and Mixers, and corporate governance weaknesses and deficiencies.  

The research also analysed the Policy implications which include the need for electronic evidence, due diligence for customers and employees to prevent money laundering/terrorist financing and effective corporate governance structures, in addition to the requirement for every person with significant control over a Digital Assets Offering Platform to, within seven days of becoming such a person, indicate to the company in writing the particulars of such control. 

To effectively address corporate governance weaknesses and the risk of exchangers of convertible virtual currencies using anonymizing features on the Digital Assets Offering Platform to move illicit funds, this research identified key recommendations that, if implemented, will provide Digital Assets Offering Platforms with the tools needed to enhance their overall control capabilities against financial crime.

title: Bank Rents, Market Structure, and Risk-taking: Evidence from U.S. Bank Holding Companies, 1995-2023

detail.title: Bank Rents, Market Structure, and Risk-taking: Evidence from U.S. Bank Holding Companies, 1995-2023
detail.abstract: We study how market-power rents, government-guarantee rents, agency costs, and competition jointly shape bank value and risk-taking. We develop a model with agency frictions in the spirit of Raith (2003) to show that these primitives affect risk through a direct profitability channel and an indirect market-structure channel. Using data on U.S. bank holding companies from 1995-2023, we find that higher rents, lower agency costs, and weaker competition increase bank value, while government-guarantee rents, agency costs, and weaker competition increase risk. Market-power rents have negligible effects on risk. Calibration of Merton-type models shows that empirically plausible franchise values are too small to constrain risk-taking, making the franchise value hypothesis quantitatively irrelevant postliberalization of cross-state restrictions.

title: Rural-Urban Inequality in Pollution Control in China *

detail.title: Rural-Urban Inequality in Pollution Control in China *
detail.abstract: Previous literature documents environmental inequality in the US. This study provides evidence of inequality in pollution control within China's regionally-decentralized authoritarian (RDA) system. A major air pollution regulation implemented in 2006 successfully lowered sulfur dioxide emissions, but less so in rural than urban counties, an important dimension of inequality in China. For every one percent reduction required for a prefecture, rural counties experienced a 0.71% lower emissions reduction than urban and a 0.35% higher incidence of illness, with no evidence of increased output or employment. Within the RDA hierarchy, inequality is not reflected in pollution goals set by the central government or sub-goals set by provincial governments, but rather emerges in prefecture-level implementation. Cost-benefit of pollution control, incentive/monitoring problems, and economic-pollution tradeoffs play some role in the goals, but do not explain rural inequality in emissions outcomes.

detail.abstract: Rare-event indicators are highly volatile in small populations, making reliable measurement difficult and contributing to the exclusion of small isolated jurisdictions from international development indices. This paper proposes a Bayesian generalized additive model (B-GAM) with empirically informed priors derived from high-income country trajectories as a method for stabilizing such indicators when cross-sectional pooling is not feasible. Simulation experiments calibrated to 62 countries show that the B-GAM substantially reduces volatility and improves accuracy across population sizes of 200 to 1,200 annual births, with the largest gains at the smallest sizes. An application to Greenland produces a smooth, interpretable maternal mortality trajectory where standard approaches yield unstable or implausible estimates. The framework offers a principled alternative to cross-sectional pooling for small and isolated populations.

detail.abstract: We propose a geometric framework to detect and forecast currency market dislocations, relying on the IG perspective of the macro-financial state variables. We employ the set of daily data from January 2010 to November 2025 to compute a curvature signal, Kt, which we obtain by rolling principal component embeddings of eight macro-financial variables relevant to the USD-JPY carry trade, namely, the spot log-return, the realized volatility, the U.S.-Japan short rate spread, the slope of the U.S. and Japan yield curves, the VIX, the deviations from covered interest parity, and a volatility-adjusted proxy of the carry regime. Kt takes negative values whenever the manifold of the market state variables exhibits concavity, which we have shown to be associated with tightening conditions, forward-spot misalignments, or constraints to global yen funding markets. We show that the negative curvature signal Kt consistently predicts the onset of all major USD-JPY carry unwind events, such as the COVID-19, the YCC stress/Fed tightening event of October 2022, the global funding shock of August 2024, as well as all historically identified yen flash events, without any false positives during periods of normal carry regimes. We also include the absolute CIP deviation, the absolute interest rate differential, and the VIX as additional regressors for the construction of the composite curvature-adjusted global risk index, GXCI-JP Y. The GXCI-JP Y has spiking activity exclusively at dislocation points, while the state space is divided into three geometrically distinct clusters corresponding to the safe, stressed, and crash regimes. We also prove the practical importance of the curvature by proposing the following simple yet transparent trading rule: long USD/JPY when Kt >-1.5 and GXCI-JP Y < 1.0, otherwise flat or short. The proposed trading rule results in an impressive 1,920% cumulative return between 2011 and November 2025, with a Sharpe ratio of 2.34 and a Calmar ratio of 19.8, outperforming the benchmark for carry, value, and momentum strategies. This proves that the information-geometric structure of the macro-financial state space has access to the leading-order information for the phase transition of the currency markets, thus providing a novel tool for the diagnosis of the risk, fragility, and carry trade of the global funding markets.

title: AI Adoption and Firm Learning in Latin America
affiliations: Yeshiva University - Syms School of Business

detail.title: AI Adoption and Firm Learning in Latin America
detail.abstract: Latin American firms face barriers to knowledge acquisition, making their adoption of new technologies such as AI particularly challenging. To counter this, Latin American centralized institutions deploy significant resources throughout innovation systems. Drawing on rational expectations, I show that individual-firm AI knowledge is key. Not only does it determine the firm's own adoption, but it also affects everyone else's adoption. The reason is that the innovation system aggregates knowledge from adoption decisions across the whole economy. However, an increasingly capable information-aggregation system can reduce total firm adoption. This seemingly paradoxical result stems from the fact that a competent innovation system may produce public information about the value of AI that is so precise that it could crowd out private learning. The crowding-out effect can be mitigated by an innovation system that accounts for individual firms' incentives to learn and places greater emphasis on directly incentivizing firm learning through cost subsidies.

The data used come from the representative survey collected in 2019 by the Centre for Affordable Housing Finance in Africa (CAHF). Based on a hedonic approach, we estimate a Conditional Mixed Process (CMP) model to consider the risks of endogeneity and unobserved heterogeneity between rental status, housing size and rent level. The results show that the structural characteristics of housing, as well as access to basic services, play a major role in shaping rents. Households in Dakar pay significantly higher rents and live in more spacious accommodation than their counterparts in Abidjan. These results underline the importance of housing quality and infrastructure in structuring urban rental markets and call for more integrated housing policies tailored to local contexts in West Africa.

title: Governing the Ungoverned: Agency Theory, Consequence Displacement, and the Financial Architecture of AI Governance.

detail.abstract: Jensen and Meckling's (1976) agency theory establishes that where ownership and control are separated, the controlling agent may pursue interests that diverge from those of the principal, generating costs that the principal cannot fully monitor or constrain. This framework has underpinned corporate governance theory and practice for five decades. Artificial intelligence systems, however, introduce a materially different and previously untheorised form of agency failure: consequence displacement. Where an AI system causes harm, the consequences are borne not by the board that authorised deployment, the vendor that supplied the system, or the shareholder that provided the capital, but by third parties-customers, children, patients, autistic learners, individuals in financial difficulty-who had no role in the investment decision and no contractual relationship with any party in the conventional principal-agent chain. Existing agency theory does not account for this structure. This paper proposes the Picken Accountability Gap Theorem (PAGT): a formal extension of Jensen and Meckling (1976) to third-party consequence displacement in AI governance contexts. PAGT identifies three structural conditions that systematically produce consequence displacement in AI deployment, introduces the Governance Internalisation Function (GIF) as the mechanism by which boards can demonstrate active accountability, and establishes the Governance Dividend as PAGT's operationally testable prediction: the annual monetary value of governance quality differential between a governed and an ungoverned operator running an identical AI system. The Picken Diamond-a fourteen-model, financially grounded board-level AI governance assessment framework-operationalises PAGT across eleven governance verticals, including financial services, cybersecurity, NHS healthcare, children's AI governance, special educational needs and disability, social enterprise, and M&A due diligence. Applied to a synthetic composite case study, PAGT predicts and the Picken Diamond confirms a Governance Dividend of £70,000 per annum on an £85,000 AI system and £287,400 in total recoverable governance failure costs. The paper makes two distinct contributions: a formal theoretical extension of agency theory to AI governance contexts, and a comprehensive, practically deployable framework that operationalises that theory. Implications for corporate governance theory, social science research, economic policy, and board-level governance practice are discussed.

detail.abstract: This thesis examines how local perceptions of economic deprivation in Thailand's Deep South reflect or challenge the claim that economic inequality plays a key role in the conflict, and whether these perceptions align with the region's economic reality. Drawing on qualitative interviews conducted across Pattani, Yala, and Narathiwat, the study centers lived experience to assess how residents interpret economic conditions under prolonged insecurity. The findings indicate that participants largely frame economic deprivation as a consequence of violence rather than its primary cause. Insecurity was described as the dominant constraint shaping labor markets, investment patterns, and everyday economic life. While the region remains economically disadvantaged relative to national averages, macroeconomic indicators do not demonstrate a singular or dramatic collapse coinciding with the resurgence of violence in 2004. This divergence highlights the limits of aggregate measures in capturing localized economic disruption. The study further finds that prolonged insecurity reshapes opportunity structures, influencing patterns of youth mobility and encouraging reliance and expansion of informal economic activity. Development initiatives were evaluated pragmatically, suggesting that state legitimacy in the region remains conditional and performance-based. By foregrounding perception, this thesis contributes to debates on conflict causation and political economy demonstrating how insecurity and lived economic experiences interact within a protracted conflict setting.

title: Correcting for the Inequality of p-Values

detail.title: Correcting for the Inequality of p-Values
detail.abstract: The conventional p-value is an inequality: it includes the probability of outcomes more extreme than those observed, making significance tests overly permissive. Using a Minimum Bayes Factor framework, this paper corrects for this inequality and derives adjusted critical t-statistic thresholds. The rule of thumb t ≈ ±2 (two-tailed, p ≈ 0.05) should be replaced by |t| ≥ 2.5, corresponding to a discrete probability of 0.015. The correction is prospective: it reduces the false positive rate for new research rather than explaining past replication failures. Roughly half of the gap between t ≥ 1.96 and the Harvey, Liu, and Zhu (2016) recommendation of t ≥ 3.0 is attributable to the inequality bias corrected here rather than to multiple testing.

title: Quantifying Euribor Manipulation Across the Term Structure: A Vector Error Correction Approach
affiliations: University of Valladolid, University of Valladolid, University of Valladolid - Department of Foundations of Economic Analysis, University of Valladolid, University of Valladolid and University of Valladolid

detail.title: Quantifying Euribor Manipulation Across the Term Structure: A Vector Error Correction Approach
detail.abstract: This paper quantifies the effects of Euribor manipulation (September 2005–May 2008) across four maturities (1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month) using a Vector Error Correction Model (VECM) that simultaneously captures long-run equilibrium relationships and short-run dynamics. We estimate that manipulation cumulatively increased rates by 1.76, 2.18, 2.54, and 2.87 percentage points for the 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month maturities, respectively. By incorporating a dummy variable for the collusion period and controlling for economic and financial factors, we recover counterfactual ‘non-manipulated’ series and re-estimate the term structure. The cointegrating relationships differ significantly between manipulated and corrected data, indicating permanent distortions in the yield curve. These findings have implications for benchmark governance, supervisory policy, and the pricing of financial contracts indexed to Euribor. Our multi-equation approach addresses endogeneity concerns inherent in single-equation models and provides the first comprehensive assessment of manipulation’s impact across the Euribor term structure.

title: ProxyDAN：Efficient Jailbreak Attack Acceleration Framework Based on Proxy Models

detail.title: ProxyDAN：Efficient Jailbreak Attack Acceleration Framework Based on Proxy Models
detail.abstract: The aligned Large Language Models (LLMs) are powerful language understand-ing and decision-making tools that are created through extensive alignment with human feedback. However, these large models remain susceptible to jailbreak attacks。Attackers can induce models to generate malicious outputs that violate alignment objectives through carefully crafted prompts. Studying jailbreak attacks not only helps reveal potential vulnerabilities in models but also provides crucial insights for building more robust security defense mechanisms. Auto-DAN, as a landmark achievement in automatically generating covert jailbreak prompts, has propelled the advancement of optimization-based jailbreak techniques. However, its attack efficiency still requires improvement.This paper addresses the high computational cost in Auto-DAN caused by the genetic algorithm's heavy reliance on model queries by proposing an efficient alternative optimization scheme. We observe that the genetic algorithm repeatedly invokes the target model for scoring during iterations, yet utilizes only its outputs rather than gradient information, resulting in substantial token and time consumption. To address this, we designed a lightweight surrogate model. By sampling response data from the target model, we fine-tuned a pre-trained language model to approximate the target model's scoring behavior. Furthermore, we proposed two hybrid evaluation strategies that significantly reduce reliance on the target model while maintaining high attack success rates.Experiments on the AdvBench dataset demonstrate that our method reduces overall computation time by 15% to 60% while maintaining attack success rates comparable to the baseline, and reduces token consumption to 20% of the original method. This research provides a new technical approach for efficient jailbreak attacks and defenses, and offers insights for lightweight design in large-model security evaluation systems.

title: MC-CoDA: Mask-Guided Cascade Attention Learning for Robust Single-Snapshot DOA Estimation Under Sensor Failures

detail.title: MC-CoDA: Mask-Guided Cascade Attention Learning for Robust Single-Snapshot DOA Estimation Under Sensor Failures
detail.abstract: Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation from a single snapshot becomesconsiderably harder when sensors in the array fail, yet reliable angularmeasurement under these conditions is critical for automotive radar, sonar,and acoustic surveillance. Random antenna outagesdestroy the covariance structure relied upon by subspace methods and introducesample-dependent aperture sparsity that conventional array processing cannothandle. This paper proposes MC-CoDA, a failure-aware deep learningarchitecture that propagates sensor health information throughout the entireestimation pipeline. The model constructs sensor-aligned tokens from complexarray observations, injects multi-scale local features through a cascadeconvolutional branch, regulates cross-sensor interaction via mask-guidedattention with a learnable geometry--health bias, and performs failure-awareglobal aggregation through mask-weighted pooling. Experiments on a uniformlinear array show that MC-CoDA delivers sub-degree accuracy acrossmoderate-to-high SNR even under heavy random sensor outages, sustains reliabletwo-source resolution at small angular separations, and exhibits the slowestdegradation among all evaluated methods as the failure ratio rises beyond thetraining cap.Ablation results identify the mask-guided attention and mask-weighted poolingas the primary sources of robustness, while the cascade local branchcontributes a complementary gain in their presence. Evaluation on measuredradar data confirms that the learned failure-awareness transfers to practicalarrays subject to unmodeled clutter and mutual coupling.

title: Enhancing Robustness of Copper Ore Sorting in DE-XRT Imaging Through Physically-Informed Thickness- Consistency Regularization
affiliations: East China University of Technology, East China University of Technology, East China University of Technology, East China University of Technology, East China University of Technology, East China University of Technology, East China University of Technology, East China University of Technology, East China University of Technology, East China University of Technology and East China University of Technology

detail.title: Enhancing Robustness of Copper Ore Sorting in DE-XRT Imaging Through Physically-Informed Thickness- Consistency Regularization
detail.abstract: In practical dual-energy X-ray (DE-XRT) copper ore sorting industrial settings, process parameters such as belt speed, X-ray source intensity, and ore particle size are typically maintained relatively stable, while the thickness of ore particles naturally fluctuates significantly due to the randomness of crushing, making it a key factor affecting sorting stability. To address the sorting instability stemming from thickness variations, this paper proposes a robust classification method centered on thickness-consistency regularization. The method is based on the X-ray attenuation mechanism, constructing logarithmic-domain thickness perturbations to simulate the input distribution shift caused by thickness variations. Experiments are conducted using a two-channel ResNet18 as the base model on 7,245 DE-XRT images, comparing three methods—Baseline, Brightness, and Consistency—and employing the Swin Transformer backbone to validate the architectural generalizability of the proposed method. Results show that Consistency achieves 92.18% accuracy on the clean test set, which is comparable to the 92.16% of the strong Brightness baseline. Under a large positive thickness shift (δ = +0.25), Consistency yields higher Macro-F1 and Worst-group accuracy, improving over Brightness by 7.76 and 11.09 percentage points, respectively. Consistency also demonstrates superior robustness over Brightness under substantial negative thickness shifts. These findings demonstrate that the proposed method effectively enhances model robustness under extreme thickness variations and is applicable to multiple deep learning architectures.

title: Prompt-Tuned Temporal Shift Spiking Neural Networks for Efficient Speech Emotion Recognition
affiliations: Southwest University, Southwest University, Southwest University and Southwest University - College of Artificial Intelligence

detail.title: Prompt-Tuned Temporal Shift Spiking Neural Networks for Efficient Speech Emotion Recognition
detail.abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) is often applied to resource-constrained edge devices. Brain-inspired spiking neural networks (SNNs) provide a new approach for studying low-power SER. If we directly apply SNNs to process the features of self-supervised learning, a serious distribution mismatch problem will arise. To solve this problem, as our primary contribution to the artificial intelligence field, we propose Prompt-Tuned Temporal Shift SNNs (PTTS-SNNs), which can compress the range of high dynamic feature values and smooth the spike frequency of neurons, improving the information processing ability of spiking neurons. In this architecture, we design a temporal shift spiking encoder, which can capture the feature information of adjacent time through parameter-free channel shifting. Additionally, we design a membrane potential calibration strategy based on spiking sparse linear attention, aggregating the global semantic context into learnable soft prompts to dynamically adjust the bias voltage of Parametric Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (PLIF) to avoid silence and saturation. In terms of engineering applications, we contribute a highly efficient and low-power SER framework suitable for edge devices. We have conducted numerous experiments on five multilingual emotion datasets and the Google Speech Commands (GSC) dataset to verify the effectiveness and generalizability. Our framework achieves the state-of-the-art (SOTA) result of 73.34% on the interactive emotional dyadic motion capture database (IEMOCAP) as far as we know, and its parameter count and energy consumption are significantly reduced. Meanwhile, we achieve 96.91% accuracy on GSC, which is only 0.01% lower than SOTA in the current SNN domain.

title: A Mass-Weighted Characteristic Function Approach to Quantifying Liberation and Heterogeneity in Gold-Bearing Ore
affiliations: University of the Witwatersrand

detail.title: A Mass-Weighted Characteristic Function Approach to Quantifying Liberation and Heterogeneity in Gold-Bearing Ore
detail.abstract: The heterogeneity of particulate materials such as gold-bearing ores poses a fundamental challenge to representative sampling and accurate grade estimation. This study introduces a mass-weighted empirical characteristic function (CF) as a model-free framework for characterising grade heterogeneity and liberation state across particle size fractions. A representative gold ore was fractionated into 14 size classes from 17.63 mm to 0.12 mm, comprising 448 individually weighed and fire-assayed fragments. The CF magnitude was computed across a frequency grid for each fraction, and a scalar liberation index, I, defined as the integral of the CF magnitude over the frequency domain, was derived. The index increases monotonically with improving liberation. The mass-weighted mean grade across all fractions is approximately 0.88 g/t, with grade variance decreasing systematically from coarse to fine fractions. A distinct inflection in I at approximately 0.88 mm identifies the practical liberation size for this ore type. A sampling nomogram relating minimum sample mass to acceptable variance is constructed from the CF-based index. The framework connects directly to Gy's Fundamental Sampling Error without imposing parametric distributional constraints, offering a generalisable, computationally tractable tool for sampling protocol design and process control in mineral processing applications.

title: Tax Notches and Household Labor Supply: Evidence from the Italian Spouse Tax Credit
affiliations: University of Amsterdam and University of Lausanne

detail.title: Tax Notches and Household Labor Supply: Evidence from the Italian Spouse Tax Credit
detail.abstract: How do tax incentives tied to spousal earnings shape behavior within households? We study an Italian policy that grants a generous tax credit to the primary earner in a couple if the spouse, labeled as the “dependent spouse” by tax law, earns below a cutoff. Using administrative tax data, we find sharp bunching at the cutoff among women, but no comparable response among men. This asymmetry is not explained by gender differences in occupational sorting, financial incentives, or other conventional barriers to income adjustment. Instead, it appears consistent with gender identity costs: the dependent spouse label aligns with traditional female roles, but conflicts with male identity norms. Women, particularly in more gender conservative contexts, persistently reduce their income and forgo job opportunities to preserve policy eligibility. Our findings suggest that gender identity norms can shape the perceived costs and benefits of tax incentives.

title: Characterizing Non-Linear Error Propagation of SRAM Bit-Flips in Convolutional Neural Networks: From Inflection Points to Fault Neutralization
affiliations: Guangdong University of Technology, Guangdong University of Technology, Guangdong University of Technology and Guangdong University of Technology

detail.title: Characterizing Non-Linear Error Propagation of SRAM Bit-Flips in Convolutional Neural Networks: From Inflection Points to Fault Neutralization
detail.abstract: We develop an algebraic analysis framework that maps transistor-level opencircuit faults in 6T-SRAM to a probabilistic bit-flip model within the IEEE 754 floating-point standard. Our analyses reveal a severe asymmetry: 0 → 1 bit flips in the Exponent domain predominantly shape the algebraic noise distribution in hidden layers. Applying this framework, we characterize a counterintuitive ”inflection point”: under extreme fault injection rates, activation saturation in bounded-activation (Sigmoid) CNNs causes accuracy to partially rebound rather than collapse monotonically. A controlled ReLU ablation confirms this phenomenon is absent in unbounded networks, which degrade monotonically to near-random accuracy. Exploiting this nonmonotonic behavior, we demonstrate a proof-of-concept for stochastic fault neutralization, achieving up to 39% accuracy recovery in controlled environments. This study provides phenomenological insights into the algebraic behavior of neural networks under hardware faults, offering a novel perspective for hardware–software co-design.

title: Robust decision-making for minimizing building life-cycle GHG emissions and costs under uncertainties: Application to office buildings in China’s cold regions
affiliations: Tianjin University, Tianjin University, National University of Singapore, Tianjin University, Tianjin University, Tianjin University and Tianjin University

detail.title: Robust decision-making for minimizing building life-cycle GHG emissions and costs under uncertainties: Application to office buildings in China’s cold regions
detail.abstract: Uncertainties can substantially affect building life-cycle assessment (LCA) results during the early-design stage. Thus, solutions selected under nominal assumptions may underperform in the future. To support robust design decisions, this study develops a probabilistic decision-making framework that integrates the 90th percentiles (P90) of life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions (LC-GHG) and life-cycle costs (LCC) with surrogate models and multi-objective optimization. The framework is applied to multistorey office-building design in China’s cold regions. The life-cycle performances of nine stock-derived building form prototypes, combined with envelope, HVAC, and rooftop photovoltaic variables, are explored under uncertain future climate, grid mix, discount rates, and component lifespans. Results show that robust Pareto-optimal solutions fall into two performance clusters mainly distinguished by HVAC energy sources. Ground-source heat pump solutions achieve LC-GHG(90%) of 22.79-23.57 kg CO2-eq./(m2·a) and LCC(90%) of 4558-5518 CNY/m2, whereas air-source heat pump solutions reduce costs by approximately 50% but increase emissions by about 30%. Within each cluster, building forms further differentiate performances, while envelope and photovoltaic choices fine-tune outcomes. Distributional analysis indicates that solutions with lower P90 values generally correspond to lower medians and narrower distributions of LC-GHG and LCC. Moreover, solutions obtained through one-step coupled passive-active optimization show similar operational emissions, with trade-offs between equipment-related embodied emissions and costs. Sensitivity analysis identifies grid mix and HVAC lifespans as key drivers of LC-GHG uncertainty, whereas discount rates and HVAC lifespans govern LCC variability. By integrating probabilistic LCA/LCC with parametric design and robust optimization, this study provides transferable guidance for uncertainty-aware decision-making in sustainable building design.

title: Modeling egg quiescence in Aedes aegypti population dynamics: effects of drought duration on viability and equilibrium stability
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Modeling egg quiescence in Aedes aegypti population dynamics: effects of drought duration on viability and equilibrium stability
detail.abstract: Aedes aegypti mosquito eggs activate a quiescent state of survival during adverse climatological drought conditions. Although this mechanism affects viability, most existing models lack an explicit link between environmental triggers of quiescence and the mosquitoes’ demographic consequences. In this paper, we developed a stage-structured, nonautonomous ordinary differential population model for several mosquito life stages, which incorporates an exponential viability reduction factor based on experimental data. Comparative results demonstrate the importance of incorporating the quiescence model in simulations. The model explains that quiescence enables short-term egg survival during drought but imposes severe population-level losses during prolonged dry periods. This corroborates the model’s stability analysis, in which the extinction equilibrium becomes stable under prolonged drought, whereas the endemic equilibrium becomes unstable. Moreover, integrating the quiescence model with the population dynamics model and environmental drivers enables a better phenomenological understanding and a more proper capture of mosquitoes’ population behavior.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and prediction of carbon emission in Shaanxi Province, China: An xLSTM-Informer framework with spatial analysis
affiliations: Xi’an Polytechnic University, Xi’an Polytechnic University and Xi’an Polytechnic University

detail.title: Spatiotemporal evolution and prediction of carbon emission in Shaanxi Province, China: An xLSTM-Informer framework with spatial analysis
detail.abstract: Traditional carbon emission forecasting models may often be difficult to capture nonlinear temporal dynamics together with complex spatial interactions among cities. To address these issues, we propose an integrated model combining xLSTM-Informer with standard deviation ellipse (SDE) and gravity model analysis for carbon emission forecasting, taking Shaanxi Province as a case study. In our method, the xLSTM-Informer model, which includes enhanced temporal memory and efficient long-sequence attention mechanisms, is first employed to characterize both short-term fluctuations and long-term dependencies. Moreover, SDE and gravity analysis are together used to capture centroid migration, spatial morphology, and inter-city spillover networks. Experimental results show that our model can achieve the best prediction accuracy among all compared methods, with an R² = 0.9528, RMSE = 6.73, MAE = 4.65, and MAPE = 8.92%. Furthermore, spatial analysis demonstrates a northeastward migration of the emission centroid and a transition from isolated urban nodes to a denser interconnected emission network. Overall, our method offers a robust and effective solution for spatiotemporal carbon emission modeling and analysis.

title: Task Computing Maximization in MEC-enabled Cell-free Networks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Izmir Institute of Technology and Izmir Institute of Technology

detail.title: Task Computing Maximization in MEC-enabled Cell-free Networks
detail.abstract: Cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) networks and mobile edge computing (MEC) are the two key enablers of next-generation wireless networks, offering enhanced connectivity, distributed and low-latency computation at the network edge. However, efficient task distribution and resource allocation are the critical challenges in MEC-enabled CF-mMIMO networks, directly impacting system performance. To address these challenges, we investigate the computing data maximization problem by optimizing the task distribution coefficients and time allocation for transmission and computing. In this work, we consider a MEC-enabled CF-mMIMO network with numerous distributed access points (APs), each of them is integrated with a MEC server, a few users (UEs) requiring to compute a large amount of data, and a central processing unit (CPU) coordinating the APs through the fronthaul. We propose two novel algorithms as the joint optimization of time allocation and task distribution coefficients (J-TATD) and load-aware weighted large-scale fading-based task distribution (LWL-TD) to maximize the computing data. The J-TATD algorithm jointly optimizes the time allocation for transmission and computing, and the task distribution coefficients, while the LWL-TD algorithm employs a heuristic approach and decouples the problem into two subproblems: i) determining task distribution coefficients; and ii) optimizing time allocation for transmission and computing using determined task distribution coefficients to maximize the total computing data. Performance evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed J-TATD and LWL-TD algorithms including the impact of task distribution by implementing an equal task distribution (ETD) for CF-mMIMO networks compared to conventional co-located mMIMO and small-cell networks.

title: LiDAR-Informed Transformer Framework for Spatiotemporal Estimation of Rotor-Effective Wind Speed Beyond Taylor’s Frozen Turbulence Hypothesis
affiliations: Pusan National University, Pusan National University, Pusan National University and Pusan National University, South Korea

detail.title: LiDAR-Informed Transformer Framework for Spatiotemporal Estimation of Rotor-Effective Wind Speed Beyond Taylor’s Frozen Turbulence Hypothesis
detail.abstract: The accurate estimation of rotor effective wind speed (REWS) is crucial in terms of improving feedforward control and enabling the effective optimization of wind turbine performance. Currently, upstream measurements provided by light detection and ranging (LiDAR) technology have been employed for REWS estimation; however, Taylor's frozen turbulence hypothesis is commonly assumed. Furthermore, effects present in real atmospheric boundary layer flow, e.g., turbulence evolution, are neglected; thus, estimation accuracy is limited. This paper proposes a data-driven approach that utilizes a transformer model to estimate REWS directly from LiDAR measurements. Through its attention mechanism, the transformer model understands the spatiotemporal information of the wind, effectively bypassing Taylor's hypothesis. LiDAR measurements are obtained from high-fidelity large eddy simulations of the atmospheric boundary layer across different wind speeds and preview distances to train and evaluate the proposed framework. The obtained results demonstrate that the transformer estimation exhibits good agreement with the target REWS values, significantly outperforming the REWS estimated with Taylor's hypothesis. The proposed model improved both the time lag and wind speed overestimation present in the LiDAR measurements. At the closest measurement gate, the root mean squared error of the estimation was reduced by 68%, 56%, and 37% for mean wind speeds of 12, 14, and 16 m/s. The findings of this study highlight the application prospects of the proposed framework in real-world wind turbine control.

title: Energy Transition and Growth-Emissions Trade-off: Nonlinear Evidence from Developing G-20 Economies
affiliations: Qingdao University, Qingdao University, Anhui University and Guangdong University of Foreign Studies

detail.title: Energy Transition and Growth-Emissions Trade-off: Nonlinear Evidence from Developing G-20 Economies
detail.abstract: The energy growth emissions nexus will continue to play a fundamental role in climate constrained development. This research uses annual panel data on Argentina, Brazil, China, India, Indonesia, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, and Turkey between 1995 and 2022, compiled using local extracts with harmonization to the World Bank World Development Indicators, International Energy Agency, and BP/Energy Institute statistical families, to estimate a panel LENARD-type error-correction model, panel threshold regression. The overall energy consumption is growth-promoting, although the impact is asymmetric: positive energy expansions are associated with an increase in output, whereas energy contractions entail more severe losses in the short-run growth. To environmental consequences, the carbon impact of power is advantageous in all specifications, yet an increase in renewable content steadily civilizes emission and undermines the power-emission elasticity when nations pass a low-renewable-share cutoff point. The quantile estimates indicate that the greatest effect of emissions is in the upper tail of the emissions distribution and the mitigating impact of renewable energy is observed in all quantiles. The additional threshold and robustness findings indicate that the early deepening of renewable does not reverse, but only moderates, the growth-emissions trade-off. G20 economies continue to experience a trade-off between growth and emissions, yet nonlinear evidence points to the possibility of incremental energy transition bending the trade-off instead of ending it. The key novelty is the clear identification of asymmetric shocks and nonlinear regimes which are not considered in the standard linear panel models.

title: MSAF-Net: A Multi-Scale Attention Fusion Network Integrating Structural Priors for Hyperreflective Foci Segmentation in OCT
affiliations: Shanghai Institute of Technology, Shanghai Institute of Technology, Shanghai Institute of Technology, Shanghai Institute of Technology, Shanghai Institute of Technology, Shanghai Institute of Technology, Wuhan University - Zhongnan Hospital, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Wuhan University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: MSAF-Net: A Multi-Scale Attention Fusion Network Integrating Structural Priors for Hyperreflective Foci Segmentation in OCT
detail.abstract: Hyperreflective foci (HRF) refers to the spot-shaped or block-shaped regions with characteristics of high local contrast and high reflectivity, which is predominantly observed in Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) images of patients with fundus diseases. Accurate HRF segmentation is clinically important but remains challenging due to their small size, diverse morphology, and embedding within complex retinal layered structures. Existing methods often struggle to model vertical retinal dependencies, integrate multi-scale features, and capture local contextual information, leading to unstable segmentation performance. To alleviate these issues, this study proposes a Multi-Scale Attention Fusion Network with Integrated Structural Priors (MSAF-Net). The network follows an encoder-decoder architecture and incorporates three dedicated modules. Specifically, the Directional Projection Attention (DPA) is designed to capture inter-layer dependencies along the vertical retinaldirection; the Spatial Context Enhancement (SCE) module to integrate global semantic information with fine-grained local details; and the Dynamic Scale Attention (DSA) module to adaptively weight multi-scale features, enabling effective fusion of structural information. Extensive experiments on the public Focis Duke dataset and a clinical RHF dataset demonstrate that MSAF-Net outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both binary and multi-class segmentation tasks. Further analyses show superior performance on ultra-small and small HRF, as well as strong robustness and generalization across cross-validation, low-HRF burden cases, and zero-shot evaluation on the OCTID-DR dataset. With moderate computational complexity, MSAF-Net provides a reliable framework for precise HRFquantification and retinal disease analysis.

title: Cross-condition and cross-chemistry battery prognostics with domain-adversarial and variance-regularized hierarchical transformers​​​
affiliations: Beijing Information Science and Technology University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Beijing Information Science and Technology University

detail.title: Cross-condition and cross-chemistry battery prognostics with domain-adversarial and variance-regularized hierarchical transformers​​​
detail.abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of lithium-ion batteries under varying operating conditions and diverse chemistries remains challenging due to complex distribution shifts in degradation patterns. This paper proposes a unified prognostic framework integrating hierarchical transformers with domain-adversarial training and variance regularization for zero-shot cross-condition and cross-chemistry battery capacity trajectory forecasting. The framework encodes SOC-aligned within-cycle measurements into compact cycle representations via a lower-level transformer with attention pooling, then captures long-range degradation dynamics through an upper-level transformer to predict future capacity. Domain-adversarial learning with a gradient reversal layer suppresses domain-specific shortcuts, enabling zero-shot transfer across unseen datasets and chemistries without fine-tuning. Variance-regularized risk minimization penalizes loss dispersion across condition-chemistry subgroups to improve worst-case performance. The model is evaluated on an aggregated multi-chemistry dataset (LCO, NCA, NCM, blended cathode, sodium-ion) under -5 °C to 60 °C and 0.2C to 6.0C. Six benchmark protocols with progressively relaxed split keys systematically assess zero-shot generalization across cells, discharge rates, operating conditions, and chemistry-domain holdouts. Results show trajectory-level MAPE of 1.02%–8.44% and end-of-life MAPE of 5.01%–9.69% under zero-shot settings, with longer observation prefixes consistently improving accuracy. Ablation studies confirm that removing hierarchical encoding, domain-adversarial training, attention pooling, or variance regularization substantially increases errors under strong domain shifts, validating their complementary synergy for robust zero-shot battery prognostics.

title: Bridging the climate to energy data gap: simulated annealing for representative climate year selection
affiliations: Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute, Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Bridging the climate to energy data gap: simulated annealing for representative climate year selection
detail.abstract: Energy system models are increasingly dependent on representative climate input. Yet, a fundamental mismatch persists between the hundreds of simulated years often used in climate science and the handful of years that computationally demanding power system models can process. Current practice, including ENTSO-E's European Resource Adequacy Assessment, relies on climate year selections that have not been validated against explicit representativeness criteria. This risks biased investment decisions and blind spots for plausible weather conditions. This study proposes simulated annealing as an optimisation method for selecting representative subsets of complete climate years from large climate ensembles. Representativeness is quantified using the seasonal sliced Wasserstein distance, a metric from optimal transport theory that captures representativeness on marginal distributions, inter-variable correlations, and seasonal structure simultaneously. We evaluate simulated annealing against the alternative methods random search, filtered random search, and K-Medoids clustering across three test cases spanning the Netherlands and Europe, using 180 climate years from the Pan-European Climate Database as a reference. Simulated annealing consistently produces the most representative subsets and outperforms all compared methods. Simulated annealing achieves an effective sample size four to five times the actual subset size. The resulting subsets are roughly 2.5-3.5 times more representative than current ENTSO-E practice. The method is application-agnostic and its output can serve as a validated climate data input to any subsequent (energy) impact study.

title: PPO-PINN: A Unified Framework for Lithium-Ion Battery Lifecycle Perception and State of Health Estimation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: PPO-PINN: A Unified Framework for Lithium-Ion Battery Lifecycle Perception and State of Health Estimation
detail.abstract: Accurate estimation of lithium-ion battery health is crucial for the safe and reliable operation of energy storage systems. To address the poor adaptability of traditional physical models to operating conditions and the lack of physical consistency in purely data-driven models, this study proposes a method that integrates Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) to enable lifecycle stage awareness. Given that battery cells exhibit different degradation pathways due to variations in environment and operating conditions, this method employs RL to dynamically adjust the activation states and weights of physical constraints. Building upon a baseline neural network that extracts temporal degradation features from batteries and constructs a multidimensional library of physical constraints, this method employs a gradient-based RL strategy known as the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm to establish a cycle-aware agent as the dynamic control center. This agent precisely detects the latent boundaries of battery degradation, autonomously identifies critical degradation stages during charge-discharge cycles, and differentially selects the most appropriate physical constraints. Experimental results demonstrate that even when trained on merely 8 cells, the proposed method achieves root mean square errors (RMSE) of 0.80% and 1.62% on lithium iron phosphate and ternary lithium battery datasets, respectively. It also maintains a low error rate (MAPE of 1.79%) under complex real-world electric vehicle operating conditions, effectively enhancing the physical robustness and generalization capability of state estimation across the battery's long lifespan and in multi-cell applications.

title: An Efficient Multimodal Transformer with Large Language Model-Inspired Components for Lithium-Ion Battery Remaining Useful Life Prediction under Limited Charging Cycles
affiliations: Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) - Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics and University of Waterloo

detail.title: An Efficient Multimodal Transformer with Large Language Model-Inspired Components for Lithium-Ion Battery Remaining Useful Life Prediction under Limited Charging Cycles
detail.abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction for lithium-ion batteries is commonly developed using long-horizon lifecycle data, whereas practical applications often provide only a few charging records, making degradation learning and model generalization highly challenging. To address this extreme low-data scenario, this study proposes an efficient multimodal Transformer framework with large language model (LLM)-inspired components for battery RUL prediction under limited charging cycles. The proposed framework jointly exploits 1D charging curves and their corresponding gramian angular field (GAF) image representations. Only five consecutive charging cycles are used as input, accounting for approximately 0.6% of the entire battery lifetime, where the 1D signals include voltage, current, temperature, and capacity. A dual-branch encoder is designed to extract modality-specific representations, with a 1D-CNN capturing local temporal patterns from charging curves and a 2D-CNN learning spatial features from GAF images. The resulting tokens are concatenated and fed into a stacked Transformer to model cross-modal interactions for RUL regression. To improve computational practicality for long-token multimodal fusion, the framework incorporates several LLM-inspired components, including FlashAttention for memory-efficient attention computation, rotary positional embedding for relative positional modeling, and a mixture-of-experts module for conditional capacity scaling. Experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently achieves superior performance under the extremely limited-data regime, highlighting its strong accuracy, robustness, and cross-dataset generalization capability.

title: Study on optimization strategy for cold start of PEMFC based on CGA-Net and HOA
affiliations: Wenzhou University, Wenzhou University, Wenzhou University, Wenzhou University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Wenzhou University

detail.title: Study on optimization strategy for cold start of PEMFC based on CGA-Net and HOA
detail.abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are regarded as a promising energy conversion technology because of their clean operation, low acoustic emission, and environmental compatibility. Nevertheless, subzero startup remains a major obstacle to the practical application of PEMFCs, because the coupled transport, phase-change, and electrochemical processes inside the cell are highly intricate and cannot be described accurately with simple analytical approaches. To address this issue, a three-dimensional multiphase non-isothermal numerical model was established for PEMFC cold start. Based on this model, a first-order finite-difference sensitivity analysis was performed to identify six dominant control parameters: namely, the initial membrane water content (), initial current density (), gas diffusion layer porosity (), catalyst layer porosity (), ionomer volume fraction (), and membrane thickness (). A convolutional neural network–gated recurrent unit–attention architecture (CGA-Net) was constructed as the surrogate model and further integrated with the Hippopotamus Optimization Algorithm (HOA) to jointly optimize these parameters. The optimization was carried out with two objectives: improving the uniformity of ice distribution in the cathode catalyst layer (CCL) and prolonging the cold-start failure time. Under the optimized parameter combination, the ice distribution uniformity index reached 0.153809, representing a 3.609% improvement over the baseline case. Meanwhile, the cold-start failure time increased to 265.35s, which is 8.746% longer than the baseline value. These findings demonstrate that the proposed method mitigates performance deterioration caused by localized ice accumulation, thereby contributing to improved fuel cell durability. The prolonged failure time further implies that ice formation is suppressed during cold start, which may facilitate faster startup in subsequent auxiliary-heating-assisted cold-start processes.

title: Probabilistic Carbon Risk Forecasting for Emerging Emission Trading Markets: A Bayesian Transfer Transformer Approach under Data Scarcity
affiliations: Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou University and Nanjing University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Probabilistic Carbon Risk Forecasting for Emerging Emission Trading Markets: A Bayesian Transfer Transformer Approach under Data Scarcity
detail.abstract: Accurate carbon market risk forecasting is essential for emission trading systems, energy sector compliance planning, carbon cost management, and low carbon investment decisions. However, emerging regional carbon markets are often characterized by short trading histories, limited liquidity, heterogeneous market structures, and policy driven volatility, which weaken the reliability of conven tional forecasting models under conditions of data scarcity. This study proposes a Bayesian Transfer Transformer framework for probabilistic carbon market risk forecasting in emerging emission trading markets. The proposed framework uses information learned from a relatively mature source carbon market to construct probabilistic prior constraints for a target market with limited data. Instead of directly transferring fixed parameters or point estimates, posterior information from the source market is incorporated into target market learning through a Bayesian transfer mechanism, allowing the model to exploit regularities across markets while retaining risk dynamics specific to the target market. A Transformer based temporal representation module is used to capture nonlinear risk evolution, while stochastic posterior inference generates both point forecasts and prediction intervals for risk assessment under uncertainty. The framework is empirically evaluated using China’s regional carbon markets, with the Hubei ETS serving as the source market and the Fujian ETS, which has limited data, serving as the target market. Carbon market risk is measured by a forward looking volatility indicator, and the input feature set includes price risk indicators, technical signals, liquidity measures, energy price variables, and compliance cycle information. The proposed model is compared with econometric, machine learning, deep learning, Transformer trained only on the target market, and fine tuned Transformer benchmarks. Empirical results show that the Bayesian Transfer Transformer substantially improves point forecasting accuracy and interval forecasting performance, particularly when training samples from the target market are limited. The 95% prediction intervals achieve high empirical coverage, indicating that the proposed framework provides useful uncertainty information for carbon risk monitoring. Robustness and ablation analyses further confirm the contributions of market transfer, Bayesian posterior constraints, and uncertainty estimation. These findings suggest that Bayesian transfer learning provides a practical and computationally tractable tool for carbon risk forecasting in emerging carbon markets, with implications for allowance procurement, regulatory monitoring, and carbon asset risk management.

title: Interaction Path Analysis and Privileged Learning Based Oscillation Risk Assessment for Multiple Wind Farms With MMC-HVDC System
affiliations: Sichuan University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Sichuan University, Sichuan University and Sichuan University

detail.title: Interaction Path Analysis and Privileged Learning Based Oscillation Risk Assessment for Multiple Wind Farms With MMC-HVDC System
detail.abstract: In wind farm (WF) transmission via modular multilevel converter-based high-voltage DC (MMC-HVDC) systems, the dominant oscillatory modes jointly established by multiple WFs and the MMC-HVDC may give rise to subsynchronous oscillations. Although the underlying mechanisms of such oscillations have been identified in prior studies, the complex interaction paths among WFs and the MMC-HVDC, as well as their impact on stability remain insufficiently elucidated. To bridge this gap, this paper develops an extended interaction path analysis method that explicitly characterizes the interaction paths between MMC-HVDC and each WF. On this basis, the mechanism through which these interactions drive unstable oscillation modes is theoretically analyzed. Furthermore, a quantitative interaction index is introduced to evaluate the interaction strength within critical frequency bands, thereby assessing the contribution of each WF to the oscillation instability risk. Moreover, a privileged-information-enhanced time-frequency network (PIETFNet) is proposed to predict the interaction index, serving as a monitoring tool for assessing vulnerable WFs during system operation. In PIETFNet, privileged frequency-domain information is distilled during training to enhance teacher network representation learning, enabling the student network to capture complex interaction dynamics using only time-domain inputs during deployment. Case studies verify the theoretical analysis of the interaction mechanism, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed interaction index, and show that the student network achieves prediction accuracy close to that of the multimodal teacher while requiring only time-domain inputs.

title: A Lightweight Reservoir Computing Approach with Multi-Scale Attention for Robust Speaker Verification
affiliations: Universidade Federal Fluminense and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Lightweight Reservoir Computing Approach with Multi-Scale Attention for Robust Speaker Verification
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a lightweight architecture for speaker recognition and verification that integrates Reservoir Computing (RC) with multi-scale and multi-head attention mechanisms. The fixed recurrent reservoir captures long-term temporal dynamics, while attention modules selectively aggregate speaker-discriminative information across multiple temporal resolutions. By restricting learning to compact projection and attention layers, the proposed RC-Attention framework significantly reduces the number of trainable parameters while preserving strong discriminative capability. The system is evaluated on three widely used benchmarks, VoxCeleb1, LibriSpeech, and CNCeleb1, covering both in-domain and cross-corpus open-set verification scenarios. Results show that the proposed model achieves competitive Equal Error Rate (EER) performance compared to state-of-the-art deep architectures, despite operating with at least 3.5x fewer parameters. An ablation study further confirms that reservoir dimensionality and multi-scale temporal aggregation are the main contributors to performance, while attention mechanisms enhance robustness and feature integration. Cross-corpus evaluations reveal strong generalization under domain and language mismatch, with consistent improvements on LibriSpeech and CNCe\-leb1. These results indicate that combining fixed temporal dynamics with lightwei\-ght attention-based aggregation provides an efficient and robust framework for speaker representation learning, particularly suited to resource-constrained and real-time applications.

title: A Preference-Driven NSGA-III Using Fuzzy AHP for Multiobjective Wind Farm Layout Optimization
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, King Abdulaziz University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Preference-Driven NSGA-III Using Fuzzy AHP for Multiobjective Wind Farm Layout Optimization
detail.abstract: Wind farm layout optimization is a complex multiobjective problem that requires balancing conflicting technical and infrastructure-related objectives while enabling effective decision-making. Although the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III) can generate diverse Pareto-optimal solutions, it does not explicitly incorporate decision-maker preferences, which often complicates the selection of practical compromise layouts. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a preference-driven optimization framework that integrates the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) into NSGA-III. The proposed NSGA-III+FAHP embeds structured preference information directly into the evolutionary search, guiding the population toward decision-relevant regions of the Pareto front. The approach is evaluated on a wind farm layout optimization problem that maximizes annual energy production and minimizes road length. Comparative results demonstrate that NSGA-III+FAHP consistently outperforms the conventional NSGA-III by producing superior trade-offs, a more structured and interpretable Pareto front, and improved decision quality without increasing computational cost, making it well-suited for practical wind energy planning.

title: Data-driven human factor analysis for oil pipeline accidents using LLM and Bayesian network
affiliations: Hebei Normal University, Hebei Normal University, Hebei Normal University and Hebei Normal University

detail.title: Data-driven human factor analysis for oil pipeline accidents using LLM and Bayesian network
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of oil pipeline networks has escalated safety concerns, yet current Quantitative Risk Assessments (QRAs) remain heavily reliant on subjective expert judgment, often failing to fully utilize complex, unstructured accident narratives. To address this gap, this study proposes a novel, data-driven analytical framework based on 5,636 oil pipeline incident reports from the U.S. PHMSA database (2010–2025). The methodology integrates a Large Language Model (LLM) with the Human Factors Analysis and Classification System based on Chain-of-Thought(HFACS-CoT) strategy, employing a direct inference-to-matching approach to automatically extract and standardize 64 hierarchical causal factors. Subsequently, a Bayesian Network was constructed using statistical screening of high-frequency causal chains and maximum likelihood estimation to reveal probabilistic dependencies and risk transmission patterns across five accident types. Results demonstrate a distinct hierarchical transmission pattern characterized by upper-level dominance and lower-level triggering. Specifically, systemic management deficits in organizational influences—such as inadequate integrity management systems—and unsafe supervision were identified as pervasive, cross-type root causes. In contrast, specific preconditions (e.g., equipment aging) and unsafe acts (e.g., illegal excavation) function as type-dependent triggers. Crucially, the findings reveal that leakages are predominantly driven by chronic systemic degradations, whereas mechanical punctures are acutely triggered by external third-party violations under regulatory vacuums. By eliminating semantic ambiguity and algorithmic hallucinations through the HFACS-CoT alignment, and by eradicating subjective bias via data-driven parameterization, this framework provides an objective, scalable tool for proactive pipeline safety management.

title: Navigating Institutional Frictions: A Longitudinal Analysis of Cross-Sectoral Policy Evolution of Forest Wellness in China
affiliations: Zhejiang A&F University, Zhejiang A&F University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Navigating Institutional Frictions: A Longitudinal Analysis of Cross-Sectoral Policy Evolution of Forest Wellness in China
detail.abstract: Given the growth of urban populations, existing literature has focused on providing evidence for the physiological and social-economic benefits of forest wellness. Yet, little is known about the role policies have played in shaping or obstructing the development of forest wellness. This paper aimed to clarify how institutional frictions occurred and were navigated in this cross‐sectoral forest wellness area. Based on a semantic-instrumental theoretical framework, this paper employed a dual‐stream thematic analysis on 81 policy and standard documents at the national level over the 30‐year evolution of China’s forest wellness sector. Through manual qualitative thematic analysis and Structural Topic Modelling, the findings reveal a three‐stage evolutionary trajectory where institutional frictions primarily arose from the misalignment between ambitious policy goals and insufficient instrumental logic. The findings suggest the state navigated these frictions through the continuous calibration of supply‐side and environmental policy instruments. Hence, forest wellness is not a linear byproduct of forest tourism expansion but a dialectical political process of state‐led adjustment. Policymakers and forest wellness managers should further emphasize on demand-side instruments so as to formally embed ecological assets into national healthcare and social welfare systems.

title: EMT-Based Dynamic Multi-Target Tracking of Magnetic Tracer Tablets via T-MSBL and Multi-Hypothesis Tracking
affiliations: The University of Manchester, The University of Manchester, The University of Manchester, The University of Manchester, Guilin University of Technology - College of Materials Science and Engineering and The University of Manchester

detail.title: EMT-Based Dynamic Multi-Target Tracking of Magnetic Tracer Tablets via T-MSBL and Multi-Hypothesis Tracking
detail.abstract: Electromagnetic tomography (EMT) represents a highly promising non-invasive approach for monitoring particle hydrodynamics in opaque pharmaceutical fluidized beds. While recent developments in Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL) have enhanced the localization accuracy of static magnetic tracers, conventional frame-by-frame reconstruction methods fail to exploit the temporal continuity of particle motion, resulting in trajectory jitter and ambiguity in multi-target identification. To overcome these shortcomings, this work presents a novel spatiotemporal tracking framework. Specifically, a Time-multiplexed Sparse Bayesian Learning (T-MSBL) algorithm is proposed to reconstruct particle trajectories by leveraging joint sparsity within a sliding temporal window. In addition, to address the label-switching problem that occurs when targets are in close proximity, a lightweight Multiple Hypothesis Tracking (MHT) strategy based on motion continuity and positional prediction is employed. Comparative experiments with both single and multiple magnetic tablets show that the proposed T-MSBL approach achieves superior trajectory smoothness and localization accuracy compared with static SBL, Kalman-filtered SBL, and recursive dynamic SBL. Moreover, results from multi-target experiments show that the motion-based MHT framework improves identity consistency and reduces ID-switching during target interaction events.

title: Geometry-Aware Multi-view Amodal Instance Segmentation via 3D Volumetric Fusion
affiliations: Beijing Jiaotong University, Beijing Jiaotong University, Beijing Jiaotong University, Beijing Jiaotong University and Beijing Jiaotong University

detail.title: Geometry-Aware Multi-view Amodal Instance Segmentation via 3D Volumetric Fusion
detail.abstract: Amodal instance segmentation (AIS) aims to recover complete object masks, including both visible and occluded regions. Existing AIS methods mainly rely on single-view observations, making reliable amodal reasoning difficult under severe occlusion. Although multi-view AIS provides complementary observations from different viewpoints, most existing methods perform fusion in 2D feature space and lack explicit cross-view geometric consistency. To address this limitation, we propose a geometry-aware multi-view AIS framework based on 3D feature lifting and volumetric fusion. Specifically, multi-view 2D features are lifted into voxelized 3D representations and aligned in a unified volumetric space for geometry-consistent feature aggregation. The fused representation is further enhanced by an attention-based decoding module that integrates bird’s-eye-view (BEV) and front-view features for visible and amodal mask prediction. A depth-aware encoding branch is also introduced to inject explicit geometric priors into the representation learning process. Extensive experiments on Movi-B, Movi-D, and MUVA demonstrate that the developed method consistently outperforms representative single-view and multi-view baselines, especially in occluded regions.

title: DOES EXPORT SPECIALIZATION SHAPE MONETARY POLICY RULES? THRESHOLD PANEL EVIDENCE ACROSS REGIMES
affiliations: Pontifical Catholic University of Parana and Universidade Federal do Paraná

detail.title: DOES EXPORT SPECIALIZATION SHAPE MONETARY POLICY RULES? THRESHOLD PANEL EVIDENCE ACROSS REGIMES
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how export specialization shapes the conduct of monetary policy by estimating nonlinear reaction functions for a panel of 31 emerging and advanced economies over 2000–2023. Using panel threshold models with the food export share as the regime-switching variable, we show that central banks in commodity-dependent economies — those with food exports exceeding approximately 30 percent of total exports — respond to inflationary pressures with an intensity roughly seven times greater than their counterparts in more diversified economies. In high-dependence regimes, the policy rate response to the unemployment gap is nearly ten times larger, consistent with the view that labor market conditions constitute the dominant signal for monetary stabilization in structurally vulnerable economies. A systematic comparison of Taylor-type and Galí-type reaction functions reveals that the unemployment gap consistently outperforms the output gap as an indicator of cyclical fluctuations in commodity-dependent settings. These findings are robust to alternative threshold variables, including the Economic Complexity Index, and to alternative detrending methods. The results carry direct implications for inflation-targeting central banks operating in primary-commodity-exporting environments, where standard linear reaction functions systematically understate the intensity of monetary responses.

title: Laboratory and season-long field evaluation of AI-based predictive control for residential heat pumps in DHW and space-heating operation
affiliations: University of Freiburg, Fraunhofer Institute for Solar Energy Systems (ISE), affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Université Paris XI Sud - CEA, Fraunhofer Institute for Solar Energy Systems (ISE), University Grenoble Alpes, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Laboratory and season-long field evaluation of AI-based predictive control for residential heat pumps in DHW and space-heating operation
detail.abstract: Residential heat pumps are commonly controlled using static rule-based controllers such as fixed heating curves and hysteresis-based DHW control, which can lead to unnecessary temperature lifts and avoidable storage losses as building and occupancy conditions change. This paper presents two AI-enabled predictive control strategies for (i) DHW production and (ii) space-heating supply-temperature control. In both cases, forecasting/modeling and optimization are separated to facilitate implementation. For DHW, a learned demand forecast is combined with Modelica-based simulation-in-the-loop scheduling that minimizes electrical energy while enforcing service constraints. Laboratory experiments show reductions in electrical energy use of 5-8% for an individual-housing configuration and 38-43% for a collective-housing configuration, together with a substantial increase in the heat-pump coefficient of performance (COP). For space heating, an attention-augmented encoder-decoder LSTM temperature predictor is embedded in a fast surrogate-assisted receding-horizon controller. A field trial in one residential building during the 2024-2025 heating season showed an 8% reduction in daily electricity use, an increase in mean COP from 3.95 to 4.15, and a reduction in mean absolute comfort deviation from 0.3 to 0.1 K. The results demonstrate that forecast-informed optimization can improve heat-pump efficiency while maintaining comfort, although broader field validation across building types and climates remains necessary.

title: TAHAN: Type-Aware Heterogeneous Graph AttentionNeural Networks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Mohammed VI Polytechnic University

detail.title: TAHAN: Type-Aware Heterogeneous Graph AttentionNeural Networks
detail.abstract: Learning from heterogeneous graphs remains challenging when structural complexity surpasses the modeling capacity of existing heterogeneous graph neural networks (HGNNs). Although current HGNNs capture structural and semantic relations, they typically treat node types as static categorical labels and overlook the contextual influence these types exert during message passing. Metapath-based models further restrict aggregation to the endpoints of a metapath, neglecting the semantic contribution of intermediate node types. As a result, they underexploit type-dependent contextual signals and often struggle in settings with sparse or weakly connected entity types. We propose TAHAN (Type-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Attention Network), a model that explicitly incorporates type-sensitive and context-dependent information into heterogeneous neighborhood aggregation. TAHAN first gathers neighbors across full metapath instances and multiple neighborhood levels, organizing them into type-specific neighborhoods. It then applies a two-stage attention mechanism: type-specific attention to capture contributions from nodes within the same type, followed by type-aware attention to model interactions across different types. The resulting representations fuse these signals into expressive, type-sensitive node embeddings. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show that TAHAN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art HGNNs. Component-level analyses further demonstrate the interpretability and practical value of type-aware modeling, offering insights for future research.

title: Comparative Assessment of RANS and DNS for Different Indoor Ventilation Regimes
affiliations: University of Cadiz and University of Cadiz

detail.title: Comparative Assessment of RANS and DNS for Different Indoor Ventilation Regimes
detail.abstract: Although Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) models are widely employed, there is a need to understand their limitations and accuracy for predicting the complex turbulent flow phenomena in indoor ventilation environments.
