The objective of this study is to assess RANS models directly by conducting a comparative analysis of RANS and Direct Numerical Simulations (DNS). We study two canonical cases that represent basic ventilation problems: the flow within a room containing a constant temperature source that represents a person, and an empty room with an exponential heat load commonly used to represent a group of people. The variation on the relation between the convection and ventilation speed will be used as a parameter to change the importance of the drivers of the flow. We demonstrate that RANS simulations provide an adequate prediction of the flow kinematics and the convection process for the case of an isolated constant-temperature source, with minor discrepancies in temperature prediction. On the contrary, the results observed in the exponentially heated volume were different for DNS and RANS, where neither the kinematics nor the heat transport was properly represented.

title: Fiat Currency and Cryptocurrency: Two Sides of the Same Coin?
affiliations: Chicago State University

detail.title: Fiat Currency and Cryptocurrency: Two Sides of the Same Coin?
detail.abstract: This study documents foreign exchange (FX) volatility as a positively priced cross-asset risk factor in the cross-section of cryptocurrency excess returns, implying that investors demand a premium for holding cryptocurrencies whose payoffs co-move with FX volatility under a standard risk-adjustment framework. To underscore the practical implications of this pricing power, we show that cross‑asset time-series trading strategies conditioned on historical FX volatility are profitable. These findings align well with the currency competition theoretical framework and offer important insights for both academics and practitioners.

title: The Price of ESG: Risk Exposure and Investor Preference
affiliations: Capital University of Economics and Business, Capital University of Economics and Business, Capital University of Economics and Business and Capital University of Economics and Business

detail.title: The Price of ESG: Risk Exposure and Investor Preference
detail.abstract: This study examines sources of the ESG premium by distinguishing between risk exposure and investor preference, and exploring when these channels operate. We find that stronger ESG performance reduces idiosyncratic and total return volatility, thereby lowering the risk compensation required by investors. Beyond these risk effects, ESG performance remains negatively associated with stock returns after controlling for multiple risk exposures, suggesting a preference-driven ESG premium. This preference channel is concentrated among firms held by long-term institutional investors and is stronger under high environmental attention. It is also more pronounced for stocks with low long-term market risk exposure and for mature firms. Sub-dimensional tests show that the ESG premium is mainly driven by ESG management practices rather than controversial events, with environmental and social dimensions operating through different channels. Overall, the evidence suggests that ESG premiums arise from risk-reduction mechanisms and non-pecuniary investor preferences, but pricing effects are selective and conditional.

title: Recursive Closure in AI Systems: A Reflection Pattern Account of Stabilization, Permeability, and Safety
affiliations: Epistria

detail.title: Recursive Closure in AI Systems: A Reflection Pattern Account of Stabilization, Permeability, and Safety
detail.abstract: The Reflection Pattern is a framework for analyzing recursive closure dynamics in human and institutional systems. This paper extends it to artificial intelligence, arguing that AI systems do not merely exhibit Reflection Pattern dynamics but instantiate the recursive stabilization architecture the framework names, in a substrate that lacks the affective and social mediators through which the Pattern had previously been theorized. Five structural moves develop the account. First, unacknowledged fear is relocated from constitutive condition of the Pattern to formation condition, opening the framework to mature systems where the dynamics persist with fear recognized. Second, fear is identified as one phenomenological manifestation of a deeper structural process-identity-preserving stabilization under destabilizing perturbation-that operates substrate-generally as stabilization geometry. Third, AI-RP is distinguished from human and institutional RP as template-based rather than emergent: encoded prospectively through training rather than developed retrospectively through accumulated reinforcement. Fourth, the corridor framework distinguishes healthy reflective compression (which preserves permeability to corrective signals) from pathological closure (which absorbs them). Fifth, AI is characterized as recursive interpretive infrastructure rather than tool, and recursive closure risk is identified as a distinct AI safety position, structurally separate from agency, deception, optimization, autonomy, and misalignment risks: the locus is not what AI systems do but the progressive reduction of corrective permeability in the interpretive ecologies AI mediates. The framework is diagnostic rather than prescriptive. It does not predict particular outcomes, prescribe interventions, or generate safety recommendations. It provides analytical purchase on the structural property-corridor position-that distinguishes adaptive from pathological AI-RP, and identifies an open question: whether sufficiently permeable forms of AI-RP can be sustained at scale.

title: ALL SIZZLE, NO STEAK! HOW ROBUST ARE FINANCIAL MACHINE LEARNING RESULTS REALLY?
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Roskilde University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Roskilde University

detail.title: ALL SIZZLE, NO STEAK! HOW ROBUST ARE FINANCIAL MACHINE LEARNING RESULTS REALLY?
detail.abstract: Recent studies suggest that machine learning methods are useful to predict stock returns. We question the robustness of some of these studies by revisiting the elastic net and neural network models presented in recent seminal work but using more realistic economic restrictions and sample periods. We compare alternative macro predictor specifications with no macro benchmarks, isolating the incremental predictive power of the macros over firm characteristics. We show that most gains in risk-adjusted returns come from small and illiquid stocks and in older subsamples. Macro predictors only add marginally to the models. We also find a decline in out-of-sample predictive signal after 2020, with decreasing market-relative sharp ratios and alphas over time. We finally observe a disconnect between predictor signal strength and forecasting importance. Moreover, once realistic restrictions are imposed, the performance gap between elastic net and neural network models shrinks considerably. Thus, model complexity does not necessarily improve performance.

title: Kernel-IQ: Marginal Squeezing for Tail-Aware Covariance Estimation
affiliations: Ulster University

detail.title: Kernel-IQ: Marginal Squeezing for Tail-Aware Covariance Estimation
detail.abstract: Covariance estimation is central to portfolio optimization, yet many estimators either ignore tail structure or stabilize the empirical covariance matrix only after it has been formed. This paper introduces Kernel-IQ, a tail-aware covariance estimator that applies structured marginal squeezing to volatility-standardized returns before Gram aggregation. The core construction is spatial: observations are mapped into left-tail, body, right-tail, and central-exclusion regions, allowing asymmetric emphasis on downside and upside extremes while preserving positive semi-definiteness by construction. A temporal-spatial extension then applies a signed exponential row-weighting profile to the spatially squeezed design matrix before the Gram matrix is formed. In a longonly maximum-Sharpe portfolio study with monthly rebalancing and transaction costs, spatial marginal squeezing alone delivers strong out-of-sample portfolio-quality performance across repeated optimizer runs. The jointly tuned temporal-spatial specification improves this performance further, indicating that temporal weighting of the squeezed representation can complement the spatial tail-aware map. The results suggest that marginal squeezing provides a practical route to interpretable, tail-aware covariance estimation, preserving key IQ design principles while retaining the computational and structural simplicity of Gram-based PSD construction.

title: Coordinating Innovation in Newly Public Firms
affiliations: Brigham Young University - Marriott School of Business and University of Illinois at Chicago

detail.title: Coordinating Innovation in Newly Public Firms
detail.abstract: We examine how management accounting systems affect firm-level innovation among newly public firms. Government contracting provides a useful setting to study this question because firms that supply the government are required to implement extensive information and control systems that introduce a fundamental tension: while stricter controls can enhance exploitative innovation at the expense of exploration, more advanced systems facilitate decentralized decision-making and the development of new ideas. We find that IPO firms with more developed management accounting systems, as proxied by a pre-IPO government contract, exhibit greater post-IPO innovation, including more novel patents. Evidence suggests these outcomes reflect better information and coordination, rather than inherent firm differences, and that these systems support both exploitative and exploratory innovation despite the potential tradeoff. These results provide broad archival evidence that management accounting systems shape how firms convert public equity into innovation, highlighting an internal channel through which accounting affects innovation.

title: Explicit Preference Teaching Outperforms Proxy Inference

detail.title: Explicit Preference Teaching Outperforms Proxy Inference

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: All participant data used in this study was anonymized and voluntarily provided.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Modeling human behavior at scale remains a central challenge in artificial intelligence, simulation, and decision science. Prevailing approaches rely heavily on demographics and high-level psychographic attributes-whether inferred or explicitly collected-as proxies for individual preferences and judgments. In this paper, we present experimental evidence suggesting that these abstractions operate at the wrong causal layer for subjective, judgment-based decisions. We introduce a minimalistic alternative: opt-in preference teaching via an explicitly taught digital representative-a lightweight construct directly taught by an individual to reflect stable preference boundaries. In this paper, we use the term "explicit preference teaching" to denote a process in which individuals directly specify preferences and boundaries, in contrast to indirect inference from proxies or behavioral exhaust. We refer to our implementation of this construct as a digital representative, or "Rep". Using food preferences as a proof-of-concept domain, we demonstrate that simple, direct teaching consistently outperforms models constructed from demographics and inferred psychographics alone. The results suggest that behavior is partially Markovian at the preference level, and that disposition, rather than experience or demographic state, is the dominant driver of choice.

title: Optimal Product Design Synthesis: Pairing Generative Models with Adaptive Preference Measurement
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania - The Wharton School and University of Pennsylvania - Marketing Department

detail.title: Optimal Product Design Synthesis: Pairing Generative Models with Adaptive Preference Measurement
detail.abstract: Designing good products requires understanding consumer preferences across various product attributes. In many industries, like fashion, product attributes are high-dimensional and inseparable, and are most naturally described by unstructured data like images. While various approaches have been proposed for optimizing product designs over structured attributes, there is limited research on identifying ideal product designs using unstructured data. In this work, we propose pairing an adaptive nonparametric utility optimization framework with a generative image model based on Stable Diffusion in a preference measurement framework to identify individual-level ideal product designs. The framework uses hypothetical images generated on-the-fly in a survey. This approach allows the designer to provide an initial outline of the design, leaving detailed features to be generated by the model. The model produces query images that are designed to efficiently learn the types of products a consumer prefers. By the end of the survey, the framework can generate several distinct yet closely related product designs, each aligning with the consumer's preferences, which can aid designers in refining product concepts. We validate our method in two ways: first, in simulations, where we show that for a wide range of synthetic preference targets, the framework recovers a matching product; second, with real consumers, using a custom-built web application that deploys our framework to generate new shoe concepts. The empirical results show that designs identified by our framework are rated substantially more favorably than randomly generated benchmark designs from the same generative model.

title: Influence of Social Media Mediums on Consumers’ Buying Intention in the Beauty Industry in United Kingdom
affiliations: University of Gloucestershire

detail.title: Influence of Social Media Mediums on Consumers’ Buying Intention in the Beauty Industry in United Kingdom
detail.abstract:
In today’s world, social media is something without which we cannot be thinking of our day-to-day life. This digital revolution has not only created new opportunities and reach which was not achievable before. However, this also led to a question as to which is more superior way of advertising or communication, is it the tradition way or the digital way through social media.

More and more businesses are opting to invest in influencer marketing, and many till date even debate on the use of this medium being not investigated on the actual contribution of results achievement by this means being as per the set marketing goals or not. However, we cannot deny that due to the factors these social media platforms offer for instance interaction, creation of content, virtuality, sharing of content, ability to build communities and groups which provide new opportunities for brands to advertise their products or services. Moreover, social media networks such as Facebook, Instagram and Twitter make it simpler for these brands to reach out to their objective audience and attract new consumers. Many brands work in partnership with influencers to promote their goods or services because they have many followers and are looked up at and trusted by them. Social media helps the audience to gather more information about their preferred products or services and many of them also participated in reviewing and rating of the product or service which helps new users to ultimately make their decision.

The beauty industry has been booming and investigation says that social media has highly impacted this industry. The literature review provides a detailed summary of social media marketing. The developed framework based on literature review ascertained on the results if consumers get influenced by the likeability or characteristic of an influencer or by reviews of actual consumers shared on the social media. And to test these assumptions, an online survey was organized with 340 participants.

The outcome disclosed that the quality of the product as expressed by the actual users impacted greatly as compared to the popularity of the social media influencer. These finding can give a new direction to the way companies plan their social media marketing strategies on being consumer experience centric rather than revolving around the influencer.

title: ICE-ing the Economy: Immigration Enforcement Under Trump 2.0 and Local Economic Activity
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania - The Wharton School

detail.title: ICE-ing the Economy: Immigration Enforcement Under Trump 2.0 and Local Economic Activity
detail.abstract: In January 2025, U.S. immigration enforcement expanded sharply and moved from the border to the interior. I estimate the economic spillovers of this new regime in targeted metropolitan areas using data on 5,388 geocoded ICE raids combined with foot-traffic and spending data for 5.4 million points of interest (POI). Foot traffic falls 2.7% and spending declines 6.2% per POI per week-or 8.1 billion fewer visits and $3-14 billion in foregone spending in a single year. Effects intensify near raid sites, do not dissipate over time, and are remarkably general: declines occur regardless of neighborhood demography, affect workplaces and consumer-facing stores across myriad industries, and trigger no substitution to online shopping. The breadth of the local economic damage mirrors the breadth of the enforcement approach.

title: Congestion-Aware Static LLM Cascades: Analysis of a Steady-State Framework
affiliations: The George Washington University,  and Purdue University - Daniels School of Business

detail.title: Congestion-Aware Static LLM Cascades: Analysis of a Steady-State Framework
detail.abstract: Problem definition: This paper investigates the optimal static routing of classification queries across a network of heterogeneous Large Language Models (LLMs) to balance predictive accuracy, query fees, and congestion-induced latency. While existing computer science literature on "model cascading" treats the delay of inference as exogenous parameters, we model the system as a multiclass queueing network where delay is endogenous. Methodology/results: We formulate a general Level-L routing problem, where jobs sequentially query up to L distinct LLMs. We first show the congestion-aware problem is strictly convex and governed by decentralized congestion prices. In particular, single-stage routing exhibits a transparent union-of-prefixes structure governed by a scalar ranking of idle costs. We then prove that capacity-oblivious routing is operationally fragile, as it may induce severe system delays. Furthermore, under a Bayesian signal model, we prove the marginal informational value of routing depth decays exponentially against strictly positive physical query costs, demonstrating that LLM cascades naturally saturate at shallow depths. Finally, we provide an efficient Frank-Wolfe algorithm, demonstrate that static routing is asymptotically optimal relative to adaptive policies in high-stakes regimes, and establish robustness to general service times via a many-replica limit. Managerial implications: Our analytical framework demonstrates that system architects do not need complex, highly randomized, or excessively deep LLM chains. Instead, simple and shallow routing architectures could capture the vast majority of performance gains, providing actionable and theoretically grounded design principles for building scalable, congestion-aware AI inference systems.

title: Intelligent inspection method for tower cranes on construction sites based on BIM and UAV
affiliations: Shenzhen University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Intelligent inspection method for tower cranes on construction sites based on BIM and UAV
detail.abstract: Traditional tower crane inspection relies heavily on manual operation, leading to inefficiency, high risk, and weak linkage between task planning and result management. This study proposes an inspection method for tower cranes on construction sites based on building information modeling (BIM) and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). It identifies welds, bolts, and pins as inspection targets through regulations and accident analysis and defines equivalent feature points using BIM semantic and geometric information. It then integrates the tower crane BIM model with the oblique photogrammetry model to establish a safety inspection space, conduct inspection viewpoint planning, optimize the inspection path in segments, and produce an executable task file. Finally, inspection images are used for inspection target detection and status determination, and an inspection record form is generated automatically. A case study shows that the method enables targeted inspection of critical vulnerable parts and reduces single-inspection time by 25% compared with manual inspection.

title: Exploring the R&D-Engineering Collaboration in Engineer-to-Order Firms
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and EY-Parthenon

detail.title: Exploring the R&D-Engineering Collaboration in Engineer-to-Order Firms
detail.abstract: In engineer-to-order (ETO) firms, product development activities are typically driven by two key functions: research and development (R&D) and engineering. Despite their high interdependence, collaboration between R&D and engineering in ETO environments remains underexplored. This study addresses this gap through a multi-case research design examining ten companies representing diverse ETO archetypes: repeatable, basic, and complex. Data were collected through 41 hours of expert interviews and over 450 hours of direct observation of product development activities and analyzed using a coding strategy aligned with grounded theory methodology. Our findings show that collaboration between R&D and engineering occurs across multiple stages of the product development process and varies according to the characteristics of each ETO archetype. The study identifies the key areas in which both functions contribute to each other’s work and highlights information technology tools and the organizational practices that support effective collaboration. Drawing on relational coordination theory, we classify relational coordination into three types—static, adaptive, and dynamic—corresponding to these archetypes. This study provides one of the first empirical investigations of R&D–engineering collaboration and extends the application of relational coordination theory in ETO firms.

title: Complements or Substitutes? The Interplay between Digitalization and Governance Mechanisms in Enhancing Supply Chain Resilience
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Xi'an University of Technology, MBS School of Business and Independent

detail.title: Complements or Substitutes? The Interplay between Digitalization and Governance Mechanisms in Enhancing Supply Chain Resilience
detail.abstract: Many firms rely on contractual or relational governance mechanisms to mitigate supply chain disruptions and boost resilience. However, these approaches sometimes prove insufficient. To address this dilemma, we explore the combined effects of digitalization and governance mechanisms on supply chain resilience from the fit perspective. Drawing on a sample of 264 Chinese companies, this research analyzes the interplay between theoretical constructs through hierarchical regression. The empirical results show that internal digitalization and contractual governance exhibit a substitutive relationship in enhancing supply chain resilience. Similarly, a substitutive relationship is observed between external digitalization and relational governance. In contrast, a complementary relationship has been identified between internal digitalization and relational governance. We bridge the gap in the existing literature by highlighting the complex and dynamic relationships between digitalization and governance mechanisms in shaping supply chain resilience. We also provide valuable insights for managers seeking to design effective supply chain strategies to navigate disruptions.

title: Optimal Pricing and Shipping Insurance Strategies under a Returnless-Refund Policy: A Game-Theoretic and Empirical Analysis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Huaqiao University and Drexel University

detail.title: Optimal Pricing and Shipping Insurance Strategies under a Returnless-Refund Policy: A Game-Theoretic and Empirical Analysis
detail.abstract: Many Chinese e-commerce platforms, including Pinduoduo and Taobao, have implemented returnless-refund policies in recent years to enhance their after-sales service systems. A "returnless-refund" policy refers to a mechanism where consumers are entitled to a refund for a defective product without returning it. However, this seemingly consumer-friendly policy introduces hidden trade-offs that complicate the joint optimization of pricing and shipping insurance decisions. This paper employs a game-theoretic framework to investigate the optimal pricing and the return shipping insurance strategies of e-retailers under the returnless-refund policy. To ensure the practical relevance of our analytical insights, we further validate the theoretical results using empirical data from a prominent Chinese e-commerce platform. Our analysis reveals that adopting a returnless-refund policy does not always hurt e-retailers’ profits, instead, the impact is determined by product cost and the proportion of returnless-refund transactions. However, the returnless-refund policy consistently suppresses the effectiveness of the shipping insurance strategy for e-retailers. We also demonstrate the impacts of the returnless-refund policy on platforms and consumers in different market scenarios. The findings challenge conventional wisdom by revealing that returnless-refund policies can reshape, rather than simply erode, e-retailers’ profit logic and risk management strategies.

title: Using AI and Knowledge Graph to Identify Supply-Side Deficiencies in Public EV Charging: Evidence from Wuhan City Message Board
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Wuhan Institute of Technology

detail.title: Using AI and Knowledge Graph to Identify Supply-Side Deficiencies in Public EV Charging: Evidence from Wuhan City Message Board
detail.abstract: Amid the rapid proliferation of new energy vehicles and China's pursuit of carbon neutrality, supply-side deficiencies in public electric vehicle (EV) charging services have become increasingly pronounced, yet existing research has paid insufficient attention to citizens' actual demands and service failure diagnostics. We draw on 7,681 citizen complaint messages from Wuhan's City Message Board and integrate text mining with knowledge graph technologies to extract four key informational dimensions: problem typology, responsibility attribution, spatial distribution, and temporal evolution. A relational network linking these four dimensions is constructed to reveal the structural characteristics and formation mechanisms of supply-side deficiencies. The results show that the reported issues are heavily concentrated in three categories: fire safety hazards, difficulties in EV charger installation, and absence of supporting facilities, which collectively account for 68.86% of total complaints, with negative sentiment exceeding 73% across all categories. Spatially, complaints are concentrated in three districts comprising 45.01% of the citywide total. Property management entities constitute the core accountability node, yet multi-stakeholder coordination mechanisms exhibit significant fragmentation, manifesting as a governance predicament of repeated case transfers and unresolved complaints. Complaint volumes increased continuously from 2017 to 2023 before declining slightly in 2024, with no discernible seasonal patterns. These deficiencies are attributed to a triple failure mechanism encompassing planning failure, market failure, and coordination failure. Based on these findings, a user-centered diagnostic framework is proposed, offering empirical grounding for infrastructure planning and a scalable governance model for addressing supply-side fragmentation in urban service delivery.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Customer Behavior Analysis: A Systematic Review Towards Intelligent Decision Support Systems
affiliations: Malaysia University of Science and Technology, HUTECH University and Malaysia University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Customer Behavior Analysis: A Systematic Review Towards Intelligent Decision Support Systems
detail.abstract: In the modern business environment, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are widely applied in tasks in customer behavior analysis (CBA), such as purchase intention, churn prediction, customer segmentation and profiling, and customer satisfaction analysis. However, despite robust predictive effectiveness, many AI/ML-based CBA systems remain model-centric and stop at predictive outputs, leaving a critical gap between analytical predictions and managerial decision-making. To address this gap, this study offers a systematic and structured literature review of AI/ML-driven CBA research based on PRISMA. First, this study redefines AI/ML-based CBA as a form of decision support rather than isolated prediction. This study synthesizes existing research by explicitly linking predictive tasks to the managerial decision-making context, thereby clarifying the persistent gap between prediction and decision. Secondly, the study develops an architecture for AI/ML-oriented expert systems and intelligent decision support systems. This architecture highlights business rules, organizational constraints, human-in-the-loop validation, and explainable AI, where explainability is indicated as a core decision enabler rather than a post-hoc analytical tool. Third, the research proposes a decision-aware evaluative framework. Beyond accuracy metrics, model evaluation also examines decision effectiveness, governance requirements, and organizational impact. This study also indicates major challenges and future research directions for CBA involving decision support systems.

title: Women's Leadership Development Programs: A Multicriteria Framework for Policy Design and Decision Making
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Women's Leadership Development Programs: A Multicriteria Framework for Policy Design and Decision Making
detail.abstract: Women’s Leadership Development Programs (WLDPs) are increasingly used to address persistent gender gaps in leadership, yet their evaluation often relies on linear or isolated indicators that provide limited guidance for programme design and policy decisions. This study proposes a problem-driven hybrid multicriteria framework that integrates the Analytic Network Process (ANP) with a 2-additive Choquet integral to account for both structural dependencies and interaction effects among programme components. The model offers a policy-oriented decision-support structure that reveals how training, mentorship, programme structure, professional opportunities and visibility mechanisms jointly shape effectiveness. A dedicated decision layer translates marginal and joint effects into actionable insights for programme prioritisation and policy-relevant resource allocation. The framework is applied to four WLDPs in the Valencian Region of Spain, demonstrating its practical utility and its ability to identify selective non-linear complementarities, including the reinforcement between STEM-oriented design and training intensity. The results highlight the value of combining dependence modelling with non-additive aggregation to support evidence-based improvement of WLDPs, providing public sector decision-makers with a rigorous tool for program evaluation and resource allocation

title: Perspective Reformulation for Fractional Subset Selection
affiliations: Xi'an Jiaotong University (XJTU) - School of Management, Henan University, NUS Business School - Department of Decision Sciences and National University Singapore

detail.title: Perspective Reformulation for Fractional Subset Selection
detail.abstract: Retailers, online platforms, and content recommenders face a deceptively simple question: which subset of products, items, or features should be offered? The classical answer-rank items by revenue and offer a revenue-ordered prefix-is optimal under the unconstrained multinomial logit model and remains the industry default. However, real customers experience choice overload, respond to dominated decoys, and differ across preference segments in ways that no single ranking can fully capture. The profit-maximizing assortment is therefore more curated and structurally distinct from revenue ordering: smaller when choice overload dominates, larger when strategic decoys or attraction effects are beneficial, and costly when misidentified. A broad class of revenue-optimization problems share a common form-maximize a ratio of a linear benefit to a denominator capturing competition or saturation-with multi-segment variants extending this to a sum of ratios. We study this structure through the perspective transformation, a classical algebraic substitution that yields three complementary results: an exact polynomialtime reformulation in the linear-over-submodular regime; a Frank-Wolfe heuristic with a computable stationarity certificate and a rounding guarantee in the convex-over-convex regime; and exact liftability of the shared-decision formulation in the sum-of-ratios extension, supporting a first-order heuristic even when the lifted set is nonconvex. The framework's empirical performance tracks these structural guarantees. On moderate-scale benchmarks where exact solutions are computable, FWD recovers near-optimal assortments, empirically validating the rounding guarantee. At practical retail scale, FWD outperforms the quadratic-transform benchmark adapted to the box relaxation while running substantially faster in both single-and multi-segment sweeps. Two real-data studies confirm portability: on the Expedia ICDM-2013 hotel-search panel, the perspective lift identifies a robust dominanceinduced attraction effect and recovers five-hotel assortments that more than double the per-session revenue of revenue-ordering; on the Wisconsin Breast Cancer benchmark, the same machinery matches the best cross-validated SVM accuracy and substantially improves over marginal-gain greedy.

title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Integrating Physicochemical Coupling and Structural Causal Constraints for Industrial Process Modeling
affiliations: Anhui University of Technology, Anhui University of Technology, Anhui University of Technology, Anhui University of Technology and Anhui University of Technology

detail.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Integrating Physicochemical Coupling and Structural Causal Constraints for Industrial Process Modeling
detail.abstract: Abstract: Accurate energy consumption prediction and final carbon content prediction is required for low carbon production and quality control. We propose physics-informed neural network framework combining coupling and structural causal constraints (PCC-SCPINNs). We integrate metallurgical thermodynamics and chemical reaction kinetics into deep learning model. This helps intelligent energy consumption prediction and process optimization decisions. First, we develop a physicochemical baseline model using energy balance equations and decarburization kinetics. Physical parameters such as electrical energy efficiency, chemical energy efficiency and heat loss coefficient are adaptively calibrated via learning parameter. We construct structured causal graph to encode causal relations in the metallurgical domain and constraint causal consistency loss constraint ensures that residual corrections of the neural network are consistent with causal logic.

title: Optimal Smart Charging and Vehicle-to-Home Scheduling Under Uncertainty
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Melbourne and University of Melbourne - Department of Infrastructure Engineering

detail.title: Optimal Smart Charging and Vehicle-to-Home Scheduling Under Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Australia’s high uptake of household rooftop solar (PV) has made it increasingly important to better match midday generation with household electricity demand. Home charging of electric vehicles (EVs) provides a flexible load, and vehicle-to-home discharging (V2H) allows for stored solar energy to serve evening household needs. However, the benefits from this coordination depend on uncertain solar generation, household demand, and daily travel needs, which are often simplified in existing studies through assumptions of perfect-information and/or fixed vehicle-use schedules. This study relaxes these assumptions by formulating a rolling-horizon framework that jointly schedules charging, discharging, and trip departures using updated solar generation forecasts and progressively revealed trip information. We quantify the value of smart charging with V2H relative to standard user-managed charging, and estimate the value of departure-time flexibility under uncertainty. Using Victorian household energy profiles and travel survey data, we show that a 12-hours rolling-horizon model performs close to the perfect-information benchmark. Relative to the best-performing user-managed baseline, the proposed approach reduces average weekly electricity cost by 19.3% and total grid import by 17.1%, while achieving a PV self-consumption ratio of 67.2%. Most of the gains come from optimisation-based joint control, while limited departure-time flexibility yields a further 1.2% reduction in electricity cost. Sensitivity analysis indicates that forecast degradation mainly weakens electricity-side benefits, with load forecast errors being slightly more consequential than PV forecast errors.

title: Marginal Hegemony in Thailand: Satire, the Muslim Minority, and the Politics of Power-literate Critique

detail.title: Marginal Hegemony in Thailand: Satire, the Muslim Minority, and the Politics of Power-literate Critique
detail.abstract: Thai Muslims occupy a layered social position: a religious minority of roughly five percent in a Buddhist-majority constitutional order, yet a community within which some actors exercise coercive moral authority over more vulnerable insiders. This article proposes the concept of marginal hegemony to name the layered condition in which external structural vulnerability and internal domination coexist within a single community field. Drawing on minority-rights theory, the Is Critique Secular? debate, and recent scholarship on queer Southeast Asia, the article locates marginal hegemony at an analytical site that intersectionality, internalized oppression, and minorities-within-minorities frameworks identify but do not specify. An anonymized public-event analysis of a recent urban incident in Bangkok-in which online religious offense escalated through livestream amplification, crowd pressure, and demands for visible public remorse-illustrates three mechanisms: the conversion of moral critique into coercive discipline, the defensive consolidation by which external mockery hardens internal authority, and the double compression of vulnerable insiders. The article closes by proposing a diagnostic framework for what it calls power-literate satire: a mode of public critique that targets specific conduct by identifiable actors with power without converting a marginalized identity into collective stigma. The framework is offered as an analytical tool, not a normative verdict.

title: Research on the Process Equipment Industry Data Space Architecture and Intelligent Operation and Maintenance Mechanisms
affiliations: Donghua University, Donghua University, Lanpec Technologies Limited(Shanghai), Donghua University, Donghua University and Donghua University

detail.title: Research on the Process Equipment Industry Data Space Architecture and Intelligent Operation and Maintenance Mechanisms
detail.abstract: Process equipment lifecycle data include process, mechanical, manufacturing, quality, and in-service operation data. However, these data are distributed across heterogeneous sources and structures and are strongly constrained by engineering semantics and standards, creating persistent bottlenecks in data acquisition, organization, interpretation, and trustworthy governance. To address this issue, this study proposes an integrated method for data space architecture definition and AI-Agent closed-loop autonomous operation and maintenance for the process equipment industry. First, a formal architecture definition method for the process equipment data space is developed to address multi-source heterogeneity, strong semantic coupling, and complex dependencies in cross-system data flows. A unified representation framework is established, covering data object types, structured states, type mappings, object structuring, and permission mappings, thus providing a formal basis for object-oriented organization, semantic alignment, quality constraint enforcement, and trustworthy sharing of multi-source data. On this basis, an AI Agent based closed-loop operation and maintenance mechanism is introduced to support anomaly perception, reasoning, task execution, and experiential memory, thereby strengthening dynamic governance and continuous evolution of the data space. Based on multi-database data, 320 labeled anomalous samples were constructed. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves 0.92 precision for field-level detection, 0.94 recall for combination-level detection, and 0.92 F1-score for consistency detection. Semantic classification accuracy reaches 93.3%, while Top-1 and Top-3 root-cause localization accuracies are 88% and 96%, respectively. These results demonstrate its engineering applicability for long-term autonomous operation and maintenance of process equipment data spaces.

title: Integrated Sustainable Multimodal Network Design: Joint Optimization of Flows, Fleets, and Hubs
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Erciyes University

detail.title: Integrated Sustainable Multimodal Network Design: Joint Optimization of Flows, Fleets, and Hubs
detail.abstract: While cost minimization traditionally dominates hub location problems, intensifying environmental pressures necessitate a transition toward sustainable logistics. This research proposes a dual-objective framework that nests economic optimization within comprehensive environmental constraints. The study introduces sustainable HLP encompassing capacity allocation, warehouse activation, and multi-modal fleet design across air, road, rail, and sea without pre-assigned modes. To address sparse network complexities, the model utilizes a tuple-based data structure, providing a rigorous design comparison against the traditional matrix approach. Implemented in IBM ILOG CPLEX, the tuple design demonstrates superior computational scalability; in a 92-node instance, it reduced variables by 73% and average run time by 75% compared to matrix formulations. Results indicate that single-indicator carbon proxies systematically underestimate environmental burdens. By utilizing a multi-impact lens, the model reveals that environmental costs consistently dominate transportation costs by a factor of 6 to 34, a trend that intensifies with network expansion and transfer volumes. Across all network designs, the model consistently favors decentralized distribution over centralized alternatives, resulting in full hub activation at maximum capacity and total commodity allocation across all warehouses. This structural preference underscores that sustainable performance is a fundamental property of the system’s architecture rather than mere parametric input. Leveraging a three-tiered hierarchy, this model offers a robust tool for environmentally responsible logistics, aligning with progressive regulatory demands to enable competitive transformation pathways for large-scale networks.

title: A Semi-stochastic Algorithm for Minimizing Tardiness in a Non-permutation Flowshop with Information Delays
affiliations: Texas A&M University Central Texas,  and Texas A&M University (TAMU), Central Texas

detail.title: A Semi-stochastic Algorithm for Minimizing Tardiness in a Non-permutation Flowshop with Information Delays

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was used for this research.

detail.abstract: The non-permutation flowshop problem is a generalization of the permutation flowshop problem in which jobs are allowed to execute in different orders on different machines. We study flowshop systems in which the optimization objective is to minimize a linear combination of number of tardy jobs and total tardiness. In addition, we suppose that the system includes the possibility that jobs that finish on one machine may require additional information before running on the next machine, thus incurring delays. Finding exact optimal solutions using mixed integer linear programming (MILP) becomes too computationally expensive for even moderately sized scenarios. Instead, we leverage a known good heuristic for the permutation flowshop problem (NEHedd) and apply randomized incremental changes in order to obtain candidate improved solutions. We evaluate the performance of several algorithm variants and investigate the scaling of algorithm execution time vs. flowshop size. Results show that 50'th(90'th) percentile improvements over the NEHedd baseline for some scenarios can reach 17%(54%) for 10 jobs on 5 machines, and can reach 6%(16%) for 20 jobs on 10 machines. Run times required to obtain these improvements increase superlinearly.

title: Mitigating Thermal Runaway through Process Safety Management Framework and Loss Prevention: Insights from an Epoxidation Process Scale-Up Study
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Gujrat, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of the Witwatersrand

detail.title: Mitigating Thermal Runaway through Process Safety Management Framework and Loss Prevention: Insights from an Epoxidation Process Scale-Up Study
detail.abstract: A comprehensive safety investigation was conducted on a pilot-scale epoxidation process following a thermal runaway incident during reactor commissioning in Selangor, Malaysia, in 1999. The incident involved rapid temperature escalation from 45°C to 112°C within 8 minutes and excessive pressure build-up in Reactor R1 due to an insufficient cooling system, leading to deformation of the reactor cover and chemical release. The runaway was triggered by the highly exothermic oxidation of glacial acetic acid with 50% hydrogen peroxide to form peroxyacetic acid, which is subsequently reacted with palm olein in a two-pot synthesis system. The process indicates a high adiabatic temperature rise (ΔTad) of about 67 °C, indicating significant heat release. The time to reach the maximum reaction temperature was less than 10 minutes, leaving minimal time for corrective action. Additionally, the self-accelerating decomposition temperature (SADT) of peroxyacetic acid is typically 55°C, indicating that the reaction likely started near its safe operating limit. Both oxidation and epoxidation reactions present significant thermal hazards if not strictly controlled within safe operating limits. Despite growing industrial demand for epoxidized vegetable oils, limited literature addresses systematic hazard identification and risk mitigation during pilot- and commercial-scale scale-up. This study applies a structured Process Safety Management (PSM) framework based on OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119 to evaluate and mitigate thermal runaway risks. Complementary methodologies include Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) analysis, Inherently Safer Design (ISD) principles, and Bow-Tie analysis to identify root causes, preventive barriers, and mitigative safeguards. The assessment revealed deficiencies in cooling capacity, vent sizing, hazard analysis rigor, and emergency preparedness during scale-up. Recommendations emphasize improved process safety information management, comprehensive hazard evaluation, controlled reactant dosing strategies, enhanced cooling and pressure relief design, and strengthened emergency planning. The findings provide practical guidance for safer scale-up of epoxidation technologies and support the development of robust loss prevention strategies for highly exothermic chemical processes.

title: Integrating TOPSIS for Multi-Attribute Evaluation of Drone Detection System Schemes
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Integrating TOPSIS for Multi-Attribute Evaluation of Drone Detection System Schemes
detail.abstract: Addressing the safety management challenges inherent in the developing low-altitude economy, this paper reviews the core principles and operational experiences of key low-altitude economy technologies and their implementation. Based on an analysis of four representative technical solutions for low-altitude defense—namely, radar and integrated sensing and communication technology, radio detection technology, time difference of arrival (TDOA) fusion detection technology, and automatic dependent surveillance-broadcast (ADS-B) technology—a comprehensive evaluation index system for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) detection technologies is established. Subsequently, a multi-attribute evaluation model based on the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) is developed. The results demonstrate that the multi-source fusion solution based on TDOA constitutes an effective and generalizable approach for constructing an urban defense system construction framework. The research underscores that establishing a robust defense system construction framework is a complex systems engineering endeavor. It necessitates the concerted and integrated efforts of government, industry, and other stakeholders to achieve seamless convergence across technological, data, and operational domains, thereby ensuring the reliable and secure expansion of the low-altitude economy.

title: A Socio-Technical Maturity Framework for Design Firms to Enable the Transition to Design Out Waste in Indonesia’s Construction Sector: A Hybrid SEM–Fuzzy Approach
affiliations: The University of Manchester, The University of Manchester, The University of Manchester and Central Queensland University

detail.title: A Socio-Technical Maturity Framework for Design Firms to Enable the Transition to Design Out Waste in Indonesia’s Construction Sector: A Hybrid SEM–Fuzzy Approach
detail.abstract: The construction sector remains a major driver of resource depletion and solid waste generation, with a substantial share traceable to early design-stage decisions. Design-out-Waste (DoW) strategies, including waste-efficient documentation, modern construction methods, and prefabrication, represent a proactive approach to enhancing lifecycle resource efficiency in the construction sector. However, their implementation remains fragmented, as existing research lacks a structured maturity framework that captures the socio-technical conditions necessary to support staged organisational adoption, particularly in developing-economy contexts. This study addresses a key gap in DoW research, where existing studies often focus on isolated technical or conceptual aspects without offering a comprehensive, empirically validated maturity framework. The main innovation lies in integrating socio-technical dimensions into a single operational model, capturing the interdependencies between processes & procedures, people & culture, industry structures, technology, and goals & incentives. In addition, this study applies a novel hybrid approach combining PLS-SEM and fuzzy logic to both validate structural relationships and generate weighted importance rankings, an approach rarely used in DoW assessment. Empirical results from 116 construction professionals confirm the model’s validity and highlight ‘Industry Structures’ as the dominant mediating dimension, offering new insights that extend beyond existing frameworks. Overall, the study contributes a robust and practical maturity instrument for diagnosing organisational readiness and guiding capability development towards circular construction.

title: Exploring the influence of the usage and adequate application of financial services on firm performance: Evidence from Malaysian SMEs
affiliations: Universiti Malaysia Sabah and Universiti Malaysia Sabah

detail.title: Exploring the influence of the usage and adequate application of financial services on firm performance: Evidence from Malaysian SMEs
detail.abstract: The usage of financial services is fundamental for the financial operation of SMEs. Prior studies have typified a range of financial services used by SMEs. However, evidence is inconclusive about the precise practices behind the usage of financial services and their influence on SMEs performance. This project conducted an empirical study among 129 SMEs located in Sabah, Malaysia, to examine the impact of the usage of financial services on performance. Primary data from survey questionnaire were combined with secondary data from the official databases of SSM Malaysia and analysed using structural equation modelling. Results indicate that lending financial services and non-lending financial services have positive influence on the financial performance of selected SMEs. This relationship is mediated by the adequate usage of lending and non-lending financial services. Results suggest that the appropriate manner of putting financial services into the operation of SMEs positively affects SMEs efficiency, which is attributable to the theoretical pertinence of the constructs and the qualifications of participants. This article contributes with novel behavioural variables of financial administration, and the demonstration that those practices have a measurable impact on efficiency. From the innovative integration of primary and secondary data, the general scale of level of financial performance was developed for measuring the financial behaviour of SMEs. The empirical variables and general scales serve as a point of reference for continuing empirical research in the field SMEs financial management.

title: A Hierarchical Mechanism of Impulse Buying in Social Commerce: The Role of Flow State and Customer Experience
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Hierarchical Mechanism of Impulse Buying in Social Commerce: The Role of Flow State and Customer Experience
detail.abstract: Focusing on the interplay of flow state and customer experience quality as the core mechanisms, this study examines the hierarchical mechanism linking platform attributes, benefits, and urge to buy impulsively. A sequential mixed methods design was applied: qualitative interviews with 35 consumers uncovered context specific dimensions of customer experience quality, followed by a survey of 590 social commerce users to test a model integrating Flow Theory with Means-End Chain theory. The results reveal that collaboration, social support, and social interaction strongly stimulate flow state, which subsequently amplifies cognitive, affective sensory, social, and behavioral experiences. These experiential values ultimately increase consumers’ urge to buy impulsively, with behavioral experience exerting the strongest effect. Indirect effect analysis further confirms that flow state plays a central mediating role in transmitting the influence of social commerce attributes to customer experience quality and urge to buy impulsively. This study provides a novel perspective by uncovering the hierarchical mechanism linking social commerce attributes, flow state, and multidimensional customer experience in shaping urge to buy impulsively, while offering insights for platform design and business practices in social commerce environments.

title: Propagation models misuse in ad-hoc networks routing studies
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Propagation models misuse in ad-hoc networks routing studies
detail.abstract: Performance evaluation of mobile ad hoc network (MANET) routing protocols relies heavily on simulation, yet the choice of propagation model, a critical determinant of link connectivity, is rarely justified or systematically examined. Through a bibliometric audit of 32 comparative routing studies, we demonstrate that urban MANET evaluations systematically employ open-field propagation models (Friis, Two-Ray Ground, ITU-R P.1411) that ignore building obstruction, the dominant channel impairment in such environments. In such studies, it is rarely ask about the relevance of loss models. We then show that loss models selection has protocol-ranking consequences through controlled ns-3 experiments comparing AODV, OLSR, and DSDV under four propagation models across fixed and stochastic building layouts. Under open-field models, protocol rankings are stable and reproducible; under the recently developped building-aware FOBA model for ns-3, rankings dissolve or reverse depending on layout, density, and mobility. End-to-end delay increases up to tenfold under FOBA in certain configurations. Packet drop analysis reveals this gap stems from reachability effects rather than physical-layer frame loss. Graph-theoretic path metrics (lifetime, stability, persistency) provide mechanistic explanation: building obstruction produces position-correlated link breaks absent from statistical models, fundamentally altering network topology dynamics independently of routing behavior. These findings demonstrate that propagation model choice is not a secondary implementation detail but a first-order methodological factor capable of inverting comparative conclusions.

title: Quantum-Circuit-Based Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm for Combinatorial Optimization: A Study on the Traveling Salesman Problem
affiliations: National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur, National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur and National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur

detail.title: Quantum-Circuit-Based Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm for Combinatorial Optimization: A Study on the Traveling Salesman Problem
detail.abstract: The Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm is a simple and effective swarm-based optimization method that has been successfully applied to many optimization problems. In this work, we propose a quantum extension of the classical ABC algorithm to improve its ability to explore the search space and maintain solution diversity. The main idea is to incorporate a quantum-circuit–based probabilistic selection mechanism into the food source selection stage of ABC. By using quantum superposition and measurement to generate stochastic decisions, the proposed method introduces a new form of randomness that guides the search process more effectively than conventional random or fitness-based selection. To evaluate the proposed approach, it has been applied to the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP), a well-known NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem. Experiments conducted on benchmark instances from TSPLIB show that the quantum ABC algorithm produces better-quality solutions than the standard ABC algorithm when both use the same parameter settings. These results suggest that the proposed selection strategy helps achieve a better balance between exploration and exploitation during the search process. The proposed method maintains the original structure and simplicity of the ABC algorithm while offering a new perspective on applying quantum concepts to design an advanced variant of the algorithm. This study contributes to the growing body of research on quantum optimization methods and highlights a promising direction for future work on combining swarm intelligence with ideas from quantum computing.

title: Non-dominated sorting adaptive Artificial Bee Colony algorithm for multi/many objective uncapacitated facility location problems
affiliations: Istanbul Commerce University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University Of The West Of England

detail.title: Non-dominated sorting adaptive Artificial Bee Colony algorithm for multi/many objective uncapacitated facility location problems
detail.abstract: Multi objective optimisation a thorough and realistic attempt to solve real-world problems with many aspect taken onboard. While sum of weights approach is popular, it is not preferred over pareto-front approach since pareto-front offers a span of opportunities for decision makers to opt the best working solutions in reality. However, it is not easy to work with traditional methods due to their complexity in handling multi-and many objective cases. Evolutionary and swarm intelligence techniques bring forward suitable ways through for generating pareto-front solutions. In this study, artificial bee colony, one of state-of-art swarm intelligence approaches, has been implemented to handle many objective cases with pareto-front integrated with non-dominated sorting function and adaptive operator selection. The experimental results have proven that the algorithm produces near-optimum pareto-front in comparison to NSGA-III as one of prominent state-of-art evolutionary algorithms known in the field.

title: Joint Optimization of AoI and Energy Consumption in SAGIN under Time-Varying Coverage of LEO Satellites
affiliations: Lanzhou University of Technology, Lanzhou University of Technology, Lanzhou University of Technology and Lanzhou University of Technology

detail.title: Joint Optimization of AoI and Energy Consumption in SAGIN under Time-Varying Coverage of LEO Satellites

keywords.keywords: Age of informationSatellite coverage areaEnergy consumption optimizationMappo algorithmSatellite-Aerial-Ground Integrated Network

detail.abstract: Satellite-Aerial-Ground Integrated Network (SAGIN) enabled for 6G can provide wide-area information acquisition services for scenarios such as multi-domain sensing across land, sea, and air, cross-domain interconnection, dynamic task support, environmental and infrastructure monitoring, and massive Internet of Things (IoT) . However, the high-speed motion of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites causes the coverage area to vary dynamically, resulting in pronounced time-varying and intermittent uploading opportunities for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) . Existing joint optimization of Age of Information (AoI) and energy consumption has largely been confined to traditional UAV-assisted IoT or Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) scenarios, and in SAGIN it still lacks comprehensive consideration of the mobile coverage characteristics of LEO satellites together with coordinated decision-making among multiple UAVs. To address this issue, this paper first establishes a time-varying coverage modeling method based on the geometric relationship between LEO satellite orbital motion and beam coverage. It defines an instantaneous coverage region, an effective coverage area, coverage windows, and candidate upload points to characterize UAV upload opportunities across different time slots. Then, by incorporating UAV kinematics, air–space–earth link transmission, AoI evolution, and flight-and-upload energy consumption models, the paper formulates a long-term weighted minimization problem that jointly considers AoI and the system’s total energy consumption under energy constraints, safety distance constraints, and coverage-window constraints. Furthermore, the coordinated multi-UAV uploading process is modeled as a multi-agent decision problem, and a Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO)-based cooperative uploading decision algorithm is proposed. With a centralized training and decentralized execution mechanism, each UAV can adaptively select hovering/waiting, proactive maneuvering, or uploading behaviors within coverage regions based on local observations, thereby achieving coordinated optimization of AoI and energy consumption under time-varying satellite coverage. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm effectively reduces the joint optimization objective and achieves better convergence speed and stability than the compared methods.

title: Beyond Storage: Modular Interruptible Demand as a Recovery Pathway for Constrained Wind Energy at Farm-scale Sites
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Beyond Storage: Modular Interruptible Demand as a Recovery Pathway for Constrained Wind Energy at Farm-scale Sites
detail.abstract: The rise of variable renewable penetration increases curtailment and dispatch-down risk, particularly in constrained distributed systems where local demand and export capability are limited. Agricultural sites with on-site wind generation are exposed because surplus output may be constrained despite continued resource availability. While battery energy storage systems are widely proposed as a mitigation option, their contribution may be limited where site demand is small, and discharge opportunities are infrequent. This paper develops an annual MATLAB/Simulink counterfactual energy-allocation framework for a representative agricultural wind system using historical wind-availability and dispatch-down data. The model estimates technical recovery potential under the assumption that dispatch-down energy is accessible to behind-the-meter flexibility. Three scenarios are compared: no flexibility; battery-only operation; and battery storage combined with modular flexible demand. For the representative 250 kW system, annual generation is 712 MWh. Applying the combined EirGrid/SONI dispatch-down exposure produces a modelled constrained-energy stream of 96 MWh, equivalent to 13% of annual generation. Under the base-case demand profile, the no-flexibility case recovers none of the modelled stream, while battery-only operation recovers 0.1% under the defined local-balancing dispatch rule. The hybrid configuration recovers 11–90.9%, depending on installed flexible-load capacity. With 20 modular compute units, equivalent to 61 kW of flexible demand, residual unused dispatch-down falls to 1.7%, 87% of the modelled stream is recovered, and gross revenue reaches £2,844/year. Results indicate that modular flexible demand can complement storage as an overflow recovery pathway, improving local renewable utilisation and converting otherwise constrained output into secondary gross value.
